lines.japanese:
気がつくと病院のベッドにいた。
　カーテンがゆらゆらとゆれている。
　外はとてもいい天気で、
　かわいた風が、夏の終わりを告げていた。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
When I came to, I was lying in a hospital bed.
The curtains swayed back and forth.
Outside, the sky was beautifully clear,
and a dry wind announced the end of summer.

lines.japanese:
「はじめまして遠野志貴くん。
回復おめでとう」
　初めて見るおじさんは、そう言って握手を求めてきた。
　にこやかな笑顔と、四角いメガネがとても似合っている。
　清潔そうな白い服も、このおじさんにはぴったりだった。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Pleased to meet you, Shiki Tohno. Congratulations on your recovery.”
A man I had never seen before said that and offered me his hand.
His cheerful smile and square glasses suited him perfectly.
So did his spotless white coat.

「志貴くん。
先生の言っている事がわかるかい？」
「……いえ。
僕はどうして病院なんかにいるんですか」
「覚えていないんだね。
君は道を歩いている時、自動車の交通事故に巻き込まれたんだ。
　胸にガラスの破片が刺さってね、とても助かるような傷じゃなかったんだよ」
　白いおじさんはニコニコとした笑顔のまま、なにか、お医者さんらしくない事を言う。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, do you understand what I’m saying?”
“No… Why am I in a hospital?” “You don’t remember.
You were involved in a car accident while you were walking down the street.
A shard of glass went into your chest. It wasn’t the sort of wound anyone should have survived.”
Still smiling, the man in white said something that didn’t sound like a doctor at all.

「……眠いです。
眠っていいですか」
「ああ、そうしなさい。
今は無理をせず、体の回復につとめるのがいい」
　お医者さんは笑顔のままだ。
　はっきりいって、とても見ていられない。
「先生、一つ聞いていいですか」
「何かな、志貴くん」
「どうして、そんなに体じゅうラクガキなんかしているんですか。
この部屋もところどころヒビだらけで、いまにも崩れちゃいそうですけど」
　お医者さんはほんの一瞬だけ笑顔を崩したけれど、すぐにまたニコニコとした笑顔に戻って、カツカツと歩いていってしまった。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“I’m sleepy. Can I go to sleep?” “Of course.
Don’t strain yourself. For now, you should concentrate on getting well.”
The doctor kept smiling.
I could hardly stand to look at him.
“Doctor, can I ask you something?”
“What is it, Shiki?”
“Why do you have scribbles all over your body? This room is full of cracks too. It looks like it might fall apart any second.”
For the briefest instant, the doctor’s smile slipped. Then it returned, as cheerful as ever, and he strode away with his heels clicking.

lines.mirrorMoon:

Can I go to sleep?"
"Yes, you should rest.
You must focus on recuperating, and not push yourself."

"Why are there scribbles all over your body?
And there are cracks, all over the walls… Why are there cracks in the walls?"
The smile vanishes for just a brief moment, then returns to his face immediately.
He turns and walks away.

lines.japanese:
「―――やはり脳に異状があるようだ。
脳外科の芦家先生に連絡をいれなさい。
それと眼球にも損傷の疑いがあるな。
午後は眼の検査に回すように」

lines.label: s20

“There does seem to be something wrong with his brain. Call Dr. Ashiya in neurosurgery. His eyes may be damaged as well; schedule an examination for this afternoon.”
The doctor whispered this to a nurse so that I wouldn’t hear.

lines.japanese:
「………ヘンなの。
みんな体中にラクガキしてる」
　くろい、ぐちゃぐちゃした線が、病院じゅうに走ってる。
　意味はよくわからないけど、見ているだけでとても気持ちがわるい。
「……なんだろう、コレ」
　ベッドにもラクガキがある。
　指で触ってみたら、つぷり、と指先が沈み込んだ。
「―――あ」
　もっと細い物で触れたら奥まで沈みそうなので、棚におかれた果物ナイフでラクガキをなぞってみた。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“How strange… Everyone’s covered in scribbles.”
Black, tangled lines ran through the whole hospital.
I didn’t know what they meant, but just looking at them made me feel sick.
“What are these things…?”
There were scribbles on the bed too.
When I touched one, my fingertip sank into it with a soft give.
“―――Oh.”
I thought something thinner might sink even deeper, so I took the fruit knife from the bedside cabinet and traced the scribble with it.

When I touch the line with my finger, my fingertip sinks down into the crack.
"---Oh!"
It seems as if I could reach farther down with something narrower, so I trace the line with a fruit knife that was lying on the bedside table.

何の力もいれてないのに、ナイフは根元までベッドに沈み込む。
　面白かったから、そのままラクガキどおりにナイフを引いた。
　ごとん。
　重い音をたてて、ベッドはキレイに裂けてしまった。
「きゃあああああ！」
　となりのベッドにいる女の子が悲鳴をあげる。
　看護婦さんたちが走ってきて、果物ナイフを取りあげられた。
lines.label: s20

It was fun, so I drew the blade along the rest of the scribble.
Thud.
The bed split cleanly in two with a heavy crash.
“Aaaaaah!”
The girl in the next bed screamed.
The nurses came running and took the fruit knife away from me.

lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“I traced that line, and it came apart. Why is this hospital covered in cracks?”
“That is enough, Shiki. There are no lines.
Now, how did you break the bed? I won’t be angry, so please tell me.”
“I told you—I only traced the line.” “…All right.
We’ll talk about this again tomorrow.”
The doctor left.
In the end, not one person believed me.

lines.japanese:
ラクガキはみんなには見えてないみたいだ。
　なぜか自分だけに見える黒い線。
　それがなんであるか、子供の自分にもなんとなく分かってきた。
　アレはきっと、ツギハギなんだ。
　手術をして傷口を縫ったあとのところみたいに、とても脆くなっているところだとおもう。
　だって、そうでもなければ子供の力で壁が切れるはずなんてない。
――――ああ、今まで知らなかった。
　セカイはこんなにもツギハギだらけで、とても壊れやすいトコロだったなんて。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
Apparently, no one else could see the scribbles.
For some reason, the black lines were visible only to me.
Even though I was a child, I slowly began to understand what they were.
They had to be seams: weak places,
like the skin where an operation had been stitched closed.
Otherwise, there was no way a child like me could cut through a wall.
――――Oh. I never knew.
That the whole world was made of seams, and was such a terribly breakable place.

lines.maoEnglish:
I didn’t want to stay in the hospital room.
I didn’t want to be anywhere covered in scribbles.
So I ran away, determined to find some far-off place where no one else would be.
But the wound in my chest hurt, and I couldn’t run very far.
When I finally looked around, I was only in a field at the edge of town.
I hadn’t made it far at all.
lines.mao_english:
I didn’t want to stay in the hospital room.
I didn’t want to be anywhere covered in scribbles.
So I ran away, determined to find some far-off place where no one else would be.
But the wound in my chest hurt, and I couldn’t run very far.
When I finally looked around, I was only in a field at the edge of town.
I hadn’t made it far at all.
lines.mirrorMoon:
I need to get out… I don't want to be in this room anymore.
I don't want to stay in a place covered in stitches.
That's why I decided to escape, and run away, to somewhere where no one else would be.
But the wound on my chest still hurts, and I didn't get very far.
That was when I noticed.
I'm standing in the grassy field just outside of town... I really didn't get far at all.

lines.japanese:
「……ごほっ」
　胸が痛くて、すごく悲しくて、地面にしゃがみこんでせきこんだ。
　ごほっ、ごほっ。
　誰もいない。
　夏の終わりの、草むらの海のなか。
　このまま、消えてしまいそうだった。
　けれど、その前に。
「君、そんなところでしゃがんでると危ないわよ」
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Cough.”
My chest hurt, and I was terribly sad. I crouched on the ground and coughed.
Cough. Cough.
No one was there.
Alone in a sea of grass at the end of summer,
I felt as though I might simply disappear.
But before I could—
“It’s dangerous to crouch there, you know.”

“It’s dangerous to crouch there, you know.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… *cough*"
My chest hurts… and I feel so sad… I collapse to my knees and cough.
*cough* *cough*
There's nobody here.
Drowning in this ocean of green at the end of summer,
I feel like I'm about to disappear.
But before that.
"Hey you.
It's dangerous to sit down in a place like that."

lines.japanese: 後ろから、女の人の声がした。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish: A woman’s voice came from behind me.
lines.mao_english: A woman’s voice came from behind me.
lines.mirrorMoon: I hear a woman's voice from behind me.
lines.mirror_moon: I hear a woman's voice from behind me.

lines.japanese:
「え………？」
「え、じゃないでしょ。
君、ただでさえちっこいんだから草むらの中でうずくまってると見えないのよね。
気をつけなさい、あやうく蹴り飛ばされるところだったんだから」
　ふきげんそうに女の人は僕を指差した。
　……なんか、ちょっとあたまにきた。
　僕はクラスでも前から四番目なんだから、そう背が低いほうではないとおもう。
「けりとばされるって、誰に？」
「ばかね、そんなの決まってるじゃない。
ここにいるのは私と君だけなんだから、私以外に誰がいるっていうの？」
　女の人は腕を組んで、自信たっぷりにそう言った。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Huh…?”
“Don’t ‘huh’ me. You’re tiny enough already; curl up in tall grass and no one can see you. Be careful. I nearly sent you flying with a kick.”
The woman pointed at me crossly.
That made me a little angry.
When our class lined up by height, I was fourth from the front, so I didn’t think I was that short.
“Kicked by who?”
“You idiot, isn’t it obvious? You and I are the only people here. Who else could it be but me?”
The woman folded her arms, utterly certain of herself.

When our class lined up by height, I was fourth from the front, so I didn’t think I was that short.
“Kicked by who?”
“You idiot, isn’t it obvious? You and I are the only people here. Who else could it be but me?”
The woman folded her arms, utterly certain of herself.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Eh………?"
"What do you mean, 'eh'?
You're already a runt so I can't see you if you're sitting in the grass.
I was this close to kicking you, so watch out."
She points at me rather grumpily.
…… I get a little angry.
After all, I sit in the fourth row from the front so I don't think I'm that short.
"Kicked?
By who?"
"Isn't it obvious, stupid?
You and I are the only ones here, so who else could it be but me?"
She declares this confidently as she folds her arms.

lines.japanese:
「ま、ここで会ったのも何かの縁だし、少し話し相手になってくれない？
　私は蒼崎青子っていうんだけど、君は？」
　まるでずっと知りあいだった友達のような気軽さで、女の人は手を差し伸べてきた。
　断る理由も見当たらなくて、僕は遠野志貴と自分の名前をいって、女の人の冷たい手のひらを握り返した。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Well, meeting here must count for something. Want to keep me company for a while? I’m Aoko Aozaki. What’s your name?”
With the easy familiarity of an old friend, the woman held out her hand.
I saw no reason to refuse. I told her my name was Shiki Tohno and clasped her cold palm.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I suppose it must be fate that we met here, so you want to talk for a little while?
My name is Aozaki Aoko.
What's yours?"
She extends her hand to me with the kind of cheerfulness one would show an old friend.
I see no reason to refuse, so I tell her my name is Tohno Shiki and grasp her cool hand in return.

lines.japanese:
女の人とのおしゃべりは、とても楽しかった。
　この人は僕の言うことを『子供だから』といって無視しない。
　ちゃんと一人の友達として、僕の話を聞いてくれた。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
Talking with her was wonderful.
She never dismissed anything I said just because I was a child.
She listened to me as an equal—as a friend.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
Talking to her was a lot of fun.
She didn't ignore what I said just 'cause I was a kid.
Instead, she listened… she listened to what I had to say, like a friend.

lines.japanese:
色々なことを話した。
　僕の家のこと。
歴史のある旧い家柄で、とても行儀作法にうるさくって、お父さんが厳しい人だということ。
　あきはという妹がいて、とてもおとなしくて、いつも僕のあとを付いてきていたということ。
　広い屋敷だから、森のような庭で、いつもあきはと一緒に友達と遊んだこと。
―――熱にうかされたように、色々なことを話した。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
We talked about all kinds of things.
I told her about my family: an old, distinguished line with a strict code of conduct and a stern father.
I told her about my little sister Akiha, who was quiet and always followed me around.
I told her how enormous our estate was, and how Akiha, our friends, and I would play in its forestlike garden.
―――The words poured out of me in a fever.

lines.mirrorMoon:

About my little sister Akiha… quiet Akiha who always followed me around.
About our big mansion and the vast gardens, and how Akiha and I would play together with our friends.
---I told her about many things almost feverishly.

lines.japanese:
「ああ、もうこんな時間。
　悪いわね志貴。
私、ちょっと用事があるからお話はここまでにしましょう」
　女の人は立ち去っていく。
　……また一人になるのかと思うと、寂しかった。
「じゃあまた明日、ここで待ってるからね。
君もちゃんと病室に帰って、きちんと医者の言いつけを守るんだぞ」
「あ―――」
　女の人は、まるでそれが当たり前だ、というように去っていった。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Oh, look at the time.
Sorry, Shiki, but I have somewhere to be. We’ll have to stop here.”
The woman began to leave.
The thought of being alone again made me lonely.
“I’ll be waiting here again tomorrow.
You go back to your room and do exactly what the doctors tell you, all right?”
“Ah—” The woman walked away as though another meeting tomorrow were the most natural thing in the world.

Sorry, Shiki.
I've got some business to take care of, so let's stop here."

"See you tomorrow.
I'll be waiting for you here, okay?
You should go back to your room and listen to your doctor."
"Oh…"
She speaks with such ease, in such a natural way as she makes her way off.

　嬉しい。

初めて、人間らしい感情が戻ってきた。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Tomorrow.”
Tomorrow, we could talk the way we had today.
I was happy.
For the first time since waking after the accident, I felt human again.

　自分の名前が嫌いなんだそうだ。
　考えたあげく、なんとなく偉そうな人だから『先生』と呼ぶことにした。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
After that, going to the field each afternoon became my routine.
The woman got angry if I called her Aoko.
She said she hated her name.
After thinking it over, I decided to call her Teach because she had such a bossy air.

lines.japanese:
先生はなんでも真面目に聞いてくれて、僕の悩みを一言で片付けてくれる。
　……事故のせいで暗くなっていた僕は、少しずつ、先生のおかげでもとの自分に戻っていけた。
　あんなに怖かったラクガキのコトも、先生と話しているとあまり恐くは感じなくなっていた。
　だから、どこの誰だか知らないけど、もしかしたら先生は本当に学校の先生なのかもしれない。
　でも、そんなコトはどうでもいいことだと思う。
　先生といると楽しい。
　大事なのは、きっとそんな単純なことなんだ。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
Teach took everything I said seriously and could put any worry of mine to rest with a single sentence.
The accident had left me gloomy, but thanks to her I slowly became myself again.
Even the scribbles that had frightened me so badly seemed less frightening when I talked to her.
I had no idea who she really was, but perhaps she truly was a schoolteacher after all.
But none of that mattered.
I was happy when I was with Teach.
Maybe that simple thing was all that mattered.

lines.mirrorMoon:
Sensei would seriously listen to anything I had to say, and would always dispel my anxieties with but a single word, without fail.
…… I was depressed from the accident, but slowly, thanks to Sensei, I began to return to my former self.
Even those scary black scribbles didn't seem quite so scary anymore when talking to Sensei.

But I don't care, it doesn't matter at all.
Because, it's fun being with Sensei.
That alone, is all that matters… and that alone is more than enough.

lines.japanese:
「ねえ先生。
僕、こんなコトができるよ」
　ちょっと驚かせたくて、病院から持ち出した果物ナイフを使って、野原に生えていた木を切った。
　あのラクガキみたいな線をなぞって、根元からキレイに切断した。
「すごいでしょ。
ラクガキが見えてるところなら、どこだって簡単に切れるんだよ。
こんなの他の誰にもできないよね」
「志貴―――！」
　ぱん、と頬を叩かれた。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hey, Teach. Look what I can do.”
I wanted to surprise her, so I used the fruit knife I had taken from the hospital to cut down a tree in the field.
I traced one of the scribbled lines and severed the trunk cleanly at its base.
“Amazing, isn’t it? If I can see a scribble, I can cut through anything there. Nobody else can do that, can they?”
“Shiki!”
Smack—she slapped me across the cheek.

「――――君は今、とても軽率な事をしたわ」

　……理由はわからなかったけれど。
　僕は、いま自分がした事が、とてもいけないコトなんだって思い知った。
　厳しい先生の顔と、叩かれた頬の痛みで。

“Teach…?”
“――――What you just did was terribly reckless.”
Teach stared at me with utterly serious eyes.
…I didn’t understand why.
But I knew that what I had just done was very, very wrong.
Her stern face and the sting in my cheek made me feel so,
so terribly sad.

“Shiki…”

“You don’t have to apologize.
Yes, you did something that deserved a scolding, but that doesn’t mean you were to blame.”
Teach crouched down and wrapped her arms around me.

lines.japanese:
「……志貴、君が見ているのは本来視えてはいけないものよ。
　『モノ』にはね、壊れやすい個所というものがあるの。
いつか壊れるわたしたちは、壊れるが故に完全じゃない。
　君の目は、そういった『モノ』の末路……言い代えれば未来を視てしまっているんでしょう」
「……未来を……みてる、の？」
「そうよ。
死が視えてしまっている。
　――それ以上のことは知らなくていい。
　もし君がそういう流れに沿ってしまう時がくるなら、必然としてそれなりの理屈を知る事になるでしょうから」
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, what you’re seeing is something human eyes were never meant to see.
Every ‘thing’ has a place where it can be broken. Nothing destined to break can ever be perfect.
Your eyes must be seeing where those things end—in other words, their future.”
“…I’m seeing… the future?”
“Yes. You can see death.
――You don’t need to know any more than that.
If the day comes when your path leads into that world, you’ll learn the reasons for yourself.”

lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Teach, I don’t really understand.”
“Good. You shouldn’t.
There is only one thing I want you to remember: never cut those lines for sport.
―――Your eyes make the lives of ‘things’ far too easy to take.”
“All right. If you say so, I won’t. And my chest hurts somehow… I’m sorry, Teach. I’ll never do anything like that again.”
“…Good. Shiki, never forget what you feel now. Hold on to it, and I know you’ll find happiness.”
Then Teach released me.

“Shiki, tomorrow I’ll bring you a very special present. I’ll give you back the ordinary life you had before.”

“Oh, that promise never to trace another line? Don’t be silly—you can break a promise like that whenever you like.”
“I can? But you said it was a terrible thing to do.”

「ええ、いけない事ね。

だからそれを使おうとするのも君の自由なの。
君以外の他の誰も、志貴を責める事はできないわ。

　君の未来にはその力が必要となる時があるからこそ、その直死の眼があるとも言える。
　だから、志貴の全てを否定するわけにはいかないわ」
　先生はしゃがんで、僕の視線と同じ高さの視線をする。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“It is wrong.
But that power is yours alone, Shiki. You are free to decide whether to use it. No one else has the right to condemn you.
Of all the abilities a person could possess, yours is exceptionally rare.
Yet if it is yours, then it must have some meaning.
God doesn’t give anyone power for no reason.
You may have those Mystic Eyes of Death Perception precisely because one day you will need them.
I can’t ask you to deny all that you are.”
Teach crouched until her eyes were level with mine.

All I'm saying is live true to yourself, and become a man in the manner that you think is right.
Since you can accept your mistakes and are able to apologize, I know that in ten years, you will become a great man."
That being said,
Sensei stands, and reaches for her trunk.

lines.japanese:
「あ、でもよっぽどの事がないかぎりメガネを外しちゃだめだからね。
　特別な力は特別な力を呼ぶものなの。
　どうしても自分の手には負えないと志貴本人が判断した時だけメガネを外して、やっぱり志貴本人がよく考えて力を行使なさい。
　その力自体は決して悪いものじゃない。
結果をいいものにするか悪いものにするかは、あくまで志貴、君の判断しだいなんだから」
　トランクが持ちあがる。
―――先生は何も言わないけれど。
　僕は、先生とお別れになるんだとわかってしまった。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Oh, but don’t take those glasses off unless the situation is truly desperate.
Unusual powers draw other unusual powers.
Remove them only when you yourself decide that something is beyond your ordinary strength, and even then, think carefully before you use what you have.
The power itself is not evil. Whether it brings about good or evil will always depend on your judgment, Shiki.”
The suitcase rose from the grass.
―――Teach said nothing, but I knew.
We were about to part.
lines.mao_english:

Remove them only when you yourself decide that something is beyond your ordinary strength, and even then, think carefully before you use what you have.
The power itself is not evil. Whether it brings about good or evil will always depend on your judgment, Shiki.”

―――Teach said nothing, but I knew.
We were about to part.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, but I must say, unless in exceptional circumstances, you shouldn't take the glasses off.
Special powers attract other special powers.
Only when you decide there is no other way should you take off those glasses, and even then, be mindful of how you use your power.
Power in itself is not evil.
What is evil rests solely in the hearts of the ones wielding such power.
Be it for good or evil, it will be up to you and the choices you make."
She picks up her trunk.
---Sensei doesn't say anything more after that,
but deep down, I knew we would have to part.

lines.japanese:
「―――無理だよ先生。
僕だけじゃわからない。
　ほんとは先生に会うまで恐くてたまらなかったんだ。
けど先生がいてくれたから、僕は僕に戻れたんじゃないか。
　……だめなんだ。
　先生がいなくちゃ、こんなメガネがあったってだめに決まってるじゃないか……！」
「志貴、心にもない事は言わないこと。
自分自身も騙せないような嘘は、聞いている方を不快にさせるわ」
　先生は不機嫌そうに眉を八の字にして、ぴん、と僕の額を指ではじいた。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“―――I can’t do it, Teach. I can’t know what’s right all by myself.
Before I met you, I was terrified. I only became myself again because you were here.
I can’t…
Without you, even with these glasses, I know I can’t do it…!”
“Shiki, don’t say things you don’t mean. A lie too weak to fool even yourself only makes the person listening uncomfortable.”
Teach frowned unhappily and flicked me sharply on the forehead.
lines.mao_english:
“―――I can’t do it, Teach. I can’t know what’s right all by myself.
Before I met you, I was terrified. I only became myself again because you were here.
I can’t…
Without you, even with these glasses, I know I can’t do it…!”
“Shiki, don’t say things you don’t mean. A lie too weak to fool even yourself only makes the person listening uncomfortable.”
Teach frowned unhappily and flicked me sharply on the forehead.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"---It's impossible, Sensei.
I can't do it… I won't understand just by myself.
The truth is, I was so afraid before I met you.
I was only able to return to being me, because you were with me…
…… I can't do it.
Not even with these glasses, if you're gone, I can't do it…!"
"Don't say such things, Shiki.
If you tell lies that even you yourself can't believe, you'll only make whoever hears you sad."
Sensei raises her eyebrows in displeasure and pokes my forehead.

mirrorMoonErrors.title: An offensive lie becomes a sad one

lines.japanese:
「―――自分でもわかってるんでしょう？
　君はもう大丈夫だって。
ならそんなつまらないコトをいって、せっかく掴んだ自分を捨ててはいけないわ」
　先生はくるり、と背を向けた。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“You already know, don’t you?
You know that you’ll be all right. So don’t throw away the self you fought to regain over some foolish nonsense.”
Teach turned her back on me.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:

You're alright now.
So don't say stupid things and give up on the self that you finally found.

Sensei turns around.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「それじゃあお別れね。
　志貴、どんな人間だって人生っていうのは落とし穴だらけなのよ。
　君は人よりそれをなんとかできる力があるんだから、もっとシャンとしなさい」
　先生は行ってしまう。
　とても悲しかったけど、僕は先生の友達だから、シャンとして見送る事にした。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“This is goodbye, then.
Shiki, everyone’s life is full of pitfalls.
You have more power to deal with them than most people, so stand up straight.”
Teach began to walk away.
I was terribly sad, but I was her friend, so I stood tall and saw her off.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Well, this is goodbye.
Listen, Shiki.
Life is not easy; everyone's life is a hard, long, rocky road, filled with many pitfalls.
You have more power than anyone else to do something about that, so pull yourself together."
Sensei is leaving.
I was sad, but I'm Sensei's friend, so I have to see her off properly.

lines.japanese:
「―――うん。
さよなら、先生」
「よし、上出来よ志貴。
その意気でいつまでも元気でいなさい。
　いい？
　ピンチの時はまず落ち着いて、その後によくものを考えるコト。
　大丈夫、君なら一人でもちゃんとやっていけるから」
　先生は嬉しそうに笑う。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“All right. Goodbye, Teach.”
“Good. That was very well done, Shiki. Keep that spirit and stay well.
Remember: when trouble comes, calm yourself first, then think everything through.
Don’t worry. You’ll manage perfectly well on your own.”
Teach smiled happily.

lines.japanese:
ざあ、と風が吹いた。
　草むらが一斉に揺らぐ。
　先生の姿はもうなかった。
「……ばいばい、先生」
　言って、もう会えないんだな、と実感できた。
　残ったものはたくさんの言葉と、この不思議なメガネだけ。
　たった七日だけの時間だったけれど、なにより大事なコトを教えてくれた。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
A wind swept through.
The whole sea of grass bowed at once.
Teach was already gone.
“…Bye-bye, Teach.”
Only after I said it did I understand that I would never see her again.
What remained were all the things she had said and those strange glasses.
We had known each other for only seven days, but she had taught me what mattered more than anything.

lines.mirrorMoon:

　僕はさよならばっかりで。
　ありがとうの一言も、あの人に伝えていなかった。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
As I stood there in a daze, tears filled my eyes.
―――Oh, what an idiot I was.
All I had said was goodbye.
I hadn’t even managed to thank her.

僕の退院は、それからすぐだった。
　退院したあと、僕は遠野の家ではなく、親戚の家に預けられる事になった。
　けど大丈夫。
　遠野志貴は一人でもちゃんとやっていける。
　新しい生活を、新しい家族と過ごす。
　遠野志貴の九歳の夏はそうして終わった。
　新しい秋がやってきて、僕は少しだけ、大人になったんだと思う――――
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
I left the hospital soon afterward.
Once I was discharged, I was sent to live with relatives instead of returning to the Tohno home.
But I would be all right.
Shiki Tohno could manage on his own.
I would begin a new life with a new family.
And so ended the summer when Shiki Tohno was nine years old.
A new autumn came, and I think I grew up just a little————

lines.japanese:
―――――秋。
　夏の面影が見事に消え去ってしまった十月もなかばの木曜日。
　自分こと遠野志貴は、八年ぶりに長く離れていた実家に戻る事になった。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
―――――Autumn.
It was a Thursday in the middle of October, when every trace of summer had vanished.
After eight years away, I, Shiki Tohno, was to return to the home of my birth.

lines.mirrorMoon:

The last traces of summer are disappearing today, a Thursday halfway through October.
This is the day when I, Tohno Shiki, return home.
It's been eight years since I left.

lines.japanese:
「志貴、早くしなさい。
いつもの登校時間を過ぎていますよ」
　台所から啓子さんの声が聞こえてくる。
「はい、いま出ますからー！」
　大声で返して、それまで自分の部屋だった有間家の一室に手を合わせる。
「それじゃ行くよ。
八年間、お世話になりました」
　ぱんぱん、と柏手をうった後。
　鞄一つだけ持って、慣れ親しんだ部屋を後にした。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, hurry. It’s already later than you usually leave for school.”
Keiko’s voice came from the kitchen.
“Okay! I’m coming!”
I called back, then pressed my palms together in farewell to the room in the Arima house that had been mine until today.
“Well, I’m off. Thank you for taking care of me these past eight years.”
I clapped my hands twice.
Carrying only a single bag, I left the familiar room behind.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki, hurry up.
You're going to be late for school."
I hear Keiko-san's voice floating in from the kitchen.
"Okay, I'm leaving~!" I call back.
I place my hands together in the room that was mine at the Arimas' up until now.
"I'm going.
Thanks for letting me live with you these last eight years."
Clap Clap.
I fold my hands together in prayer.
Then, grabbing my only bag, I leave the room that had become so familiar.

lines.japanese:
玄関を出て、有間の屋敷を振りかえる。
「志貴」
　玄関口まで見送りにきた啓子さんは、淋しそうな目で俺の名前を口にした。
「行ってきます。
母さんも元気で」
　もう帰ってくる事はないのに行ってきます、というのはおかしかった。
　もうこの先、家族としてこの家の敷居をまたぐ事はないんだから。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
Outside the front door, I turned to look back at the Arima house.
“Shiki.”
Keiko had come to see me off, and there was sadness in her eyes as she spoke my name.
“See you later. Take care, Mom.”
It was strange to say see you later when I would never be coming back.
Never again would I cross that threshold as a member of the family.

"See you later.
Take care, Mom."
What a strange thing to say.
I won't be coming back.
Never again will I pass through this door as a member of the Arima family.

lines.japanese:
「今までお世話になりました。
父さんにもよろしく言っておいてください」
　啓子さんはただうなずくだけだった。
　八年間────俺の母親であった人は、ひどく悲しげな目をしていた。
　この人のそんな顔、今まで見たことはなかったと思う。
「遠野の屋敷の生活はたいへんでしょうけど、しっかりね。
あなたは体が弱いのだから、あまり無茶をしてはいけませんよ」
「大丈夫、八年もたてば人並みに健康な体に戻ります。
こう見えてもワリと頑丈なんです、俺の体」
「ええ、そうだったわね。
けど遠野の方達はみなどこか違っている人達ですから、志貴が圧倒されないかと心配で」
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Thank you for everything. Please give Dad my best.”
Keiko only nodded.
The woman who had been my mother for eight years looked heartbroken.
I didn’t think I had ever seen that expression on her face before.
“Life at the Tohno estate won’t be easy, but do your best. You’ve always been frail, so please don’t push yourself too hard.”
“I’m fine. Eight years is long enough to get as healthy as anyone else. I’m sturdier than I look.”
“Yes, I suppose you are. But the people at the Tohno house are all somehow… different. I’m afraid they may overwhelm you.”

Your body is weak; you mustn't overdo it."
"I'll be okay.
After eight years, I'm just as healthy as anyone else.
I'm a lot tougher than I look."
"I suppose you're right.
But… the Tohnos are different from everyone else.
I'm worried they'll be too much for you."

lines.japanese:
啓子さんの言いたい事はなんとなくわかる。
　今日から俺が住む事になる家は、お屋敷ともいえる時代錯誤な建物なのだ。
　住んでる家も立派なら家柄も立派という名家で、実際いくつかの会社の株主でもあるらしい。
　くわえて言うのなら、八年前に長男である俺―――遠野志貴を親戚である有間の家に預けた、自分にとって本当の家でもある。
「でも、もう決めた事ですから」
　そう、もう決めた事だった。
「……それじゃあ行ってきます。
今までお世話になりました」
　最後にもう一度だけそう言って、八年間馴れしたんだ有間の家を後にした。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
I had some idea what Keiko meant.
The place I would move into today was a vast, hopelessly anachronistic estate.
It belonged to an old and distinguished family, apparently a shareholder in several companies.
More to the point, it was my true home—the house that had sent its eldest son, Shiki Tohno, to live with our relatives, the Arimas, eight years ago.
“But it’s already been decided.”
And it had.
“…Well, I’m off. Thank you for everything.”
I said it one last time, then left the Arima home where I had spent the past eight years.

Yeah, it's something that's decided already.
"Alright, I'll be heading off then.
Thanks for taking care of me."
I repeat those words one last time, and turn my back on the household I had grown so accustomed to over these past eight years.

「――――はあ」
　有間の家から離れて、いつもの通学路に出たとたん、気が重くなった。
―――八年前。
　普通なら即死、という重症から回復した俺は、親元である遠野の家から分家筋である有間の家に預けられた。
　俺は九歳までは実の両親の家である遠野の屋敷で暮らしていて、
　その後の八年間、
　高校二年生である今までを親戚である有間の家で暮らしていた、というコトになる。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Haaah…”
The instant I left the Arima house behind and reached my usual route to school, my spirits sank.
―――Eight years ago.
After recovering from injuries that should have killed me instantly, I was sent from the main Tohno family to live with the Arimas, one of its branch families.
I had lived with my birth parents at the Tohno estate until I was nine,
then spent the next eight years with my relatives, the Arimas,
right up to my second year of high school.

lines.mirrorMoon:

lines.japanese:
なかば養子という形で有間の家に預けられてからの生活は、いたってノーマルなものだった。
　あの時―――別れ際に先生が言っていたような特別な出来事はまったくおこらなかったし、自分も先生のくれたメガネをかけているかぎり『線』を見る事がない。
　遠野志貴の生活は、本当に平凡に。
　とても穏やかなままで、ゆるやかに流れていた。
　……つい先日。
　今まで勘当同然に放っておかれた自分に、
　　　『今日までに遠野の屋敷に戻って来い』
　なんていう遠野家当主からのお言葉がくるまでは。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
My life after being placed with the Arimas, almost as an adopted son, was thoroughly normal.
Nothing like the extraordinary events Teach had warned about when we parted ever happened, and as long as I wore the glasses she had given me, I never saw the lines.
Shiki Tohno’s life was utterly ordinary.
It flowed on, quiet and unhurried.
…Until a few days ago,
when the son they had all but disowned
received an order from the head of the Tohno family:
“Return to the Tohno estate by today.”

lines.mirrorMoon:

From the time I met Sensei---those special circumstances Sensei told me about as she parted never happened, and the glasses hid the "lines" from me as long as I wore them.
The life of Tohno Shiki was a peaceful one.
It meandered along gently…
…… until a few days ago.
The day when the head of the Tohno family sent word to me.
"Return to the Tohno Mansion."
The very family that, until now, had shunned me.

「はあ────」
　またため息がでる。
　実のところ、交通事故に巻き込まれて入院する以前から、俺は遠野の家とは折り合いが悪かった。
　行儀作法にうるさい屋敷の生活が子供心にはつまらないモノに思えてしまったせいだろう。
　だから有間の家に預ける、と実の父親に言われた時は、さして抵抗もなく養子に出た。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Haaah…”
Another sigh escaped me.
Truthfully, I had never got along with the Tohno household, even before the traffic accident put me in the hospital.
To a child, life in a mansion obsessed with manners had simply seemed boring.
So when my father told me I was being sent to the Arimas, I had gone with hardly any resistance.

lines.mirrorMoon:

Maybe as a kid I never liked the formality demanded by the family.
Perhaps that's why I said nothing when the old man told me I was going to live with the Arimas.

lines.japanese:
結果は、とても良好だったと思う。
　有間の家の人たちとは上手くやっていけたし、義理の母親である啓子さんとも、義理の父親である文臣さんとも親子のように接してきた。
　もともと一般的な温かい家庭に憧れていたところもあって、遠野志貴は有間の家で本当の子供のように暮らしてきた。
　そこに後悔のたぐいはまったくなかった。
　……ただ一つ。
　一歳年下の妹を遠野の屋敷に残してきてしまった、ということ以外は。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
I thought it had worked out wonderfully.
I got along with the Arima family, and Keiko and Fumiomi, my foster mother and father, treated me as their own son.
I had always longed for an ordinary, loving home, and Shiki Tohno had lived as a true child of the Arima family.
I regretted none of it.
…Except for one thing:
I had left my little sister, one year younger than me, behind at the Tohno estate.

lines.mirrorMoon:

I don't regret living there.

…… Except for one thing.
My little sister, one year younger than me, remained behind with the Tohnos.

lines.japanese:
「……秋葉のやつ、俺のことを恨んでるんだろうな」
　というか、恨まれて当然のような気がする。
　あの、やたら広い屋敷に一人きりになって、頭の硬い父親とつきっきりで暮らしていたんだ。
　秋葉がさっさと外に逃げ出してしまった俺のことをどう思っているかは容易に想像できる。
「…………はあ」
　ため息をついても仕方がない。
　あとはもうなるようになれだ。
　今日、学校が終わったら八年ぶりに実家に帰る。
そこで何が待っているかは神のみぞ知るというところだろう。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Akiha must hate me.”
In fact, she had every right to.
She had been left alone in that absurdly vast mansion, living under the constant eye of our inflexible father.
It was easy to imagine what she thought of the brother who had escaped at the first opportunity.
“…Haaah.”
Sighing wouldn’t help.
Whatever happened would happen.
After school today, I would return home for the first time in eight years. Only God knew what would be waiting for me there.

I let out another sigh.
I can't help it.
What's going to happen will happen.
Today, after school, I'll return to my true home.
Lord knows what'll occur.

「そうだよな。
それに今はもっと切迫した問題があるし」
　腕時計は七時四十五分をさしている。
　うちの高校は八時きっかりに朝のホームルームが始まるため、八時までに教室にいないと遅刻が確定してしまう。
　鞄を抱えて、学校までダッシュする事にした。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Right. And I have a more urgent problem at the moment.”
My watch read seven forty-five.
Morning homeroom began at eight sharp, which meant that if I wasn’t in my classroom by then, I was officially late.
I hugged my bag to my chest and sprinted for school.

lines.mirrorMoon:

lines.japanese:
「ハア、ハア、ハア――――」
　着いた。
　家から学校まで実に十分弱。
　陸上部がスカウトにこないのが不思議なぐらいの好タイムをたたき出して、裏門から校庭に入る。
「……そっか。
裏門から入るのも今日で最後か」
　位置的に有間の家と遠野の家は学校を挟んで正反対の場所にある。
　有間の家は学校の裏側に、遠野の屋敷は学校の正門方向。
　自然、明日からの登校口は裏門ではなく正門からになるだろう。
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah, hah――――”
I made it.
Home to school in just under ten minutes.
It was fast enough to make me wonder why the track team had never tried to recruit me, and I entered the grounds through the back gate.
“—Oh. I guess this is the last time I’ll come in this way.”
The Arima and Tohno homes stood on opposite sides of the school.
The Arima house lay behind it; the Tohno estate, beyond the main gate.
Starting tomorrow, I would naturally be coming through the front.

「ここの寂しい雰囲気、わりと好きだったんだけどな」
　なぜかうちの高校の裏門は不人気で、利用しているのは自分をふくめて十人たらずしかいない。
　そのせいか、裏庭は朝夕問わずに静かな、人気のない場所になっている。
　かーん、かか、かーん。
　……だからだろうか。
　小鳥のさえずりに混ざって、トンカチの音まで確かに聞き取れてしまうのは。
「トンカチの音か―――って、え……？」
lines.label: s20
lines.maoEnglish:
“I rather liked how lonely it felt back here.”
For some reason, our school’s back gate was unpopular. Fewer than ten students used it, myself included.
As a result, the rear grounds remained quiet and deserted, morning and evening alike.
Clang, cl-cl, clang.
…Maybe that was why:
I could hear the hammer clearly even through the birdsong.
“Hammering—wait, what…?”

Clink, Clink, Clang!
…… Like I said, pretty quiet.

"Hammering… Huh?"

　少なくとも自分は八年前───九歳まで遠野の屋敷で暮らしていたから、屋敷へ帰る道は初めてというわけでもないのだ。
lines.label: s201
lines.maoEnglish:

Unknown streets carried me steadily closer to the Tohno estate.
Yet the scenery around them was not entirely unfamiliar.
I had lived at the estate until I was nine───eight years ago, so this was not truly my first journey home.

lines.japanese:
母親は秋葉が生まれた時に病死してしまっていたから、遠野の人間は自分と、妹である秋葉の二人きりになってしまった。
　本来なら長男である自分───遠野志貴が遠野家の跡取りになるのだろうけれど、自分にはそんな権利はない。
lines.label: s201
lines.maoEnglish:
Our mother had died of illness when Akiha was born, so my sister and I were now the only Tohnos left.
Ordinarily, I───Shiki Tohno, the eldest son, would have inherited the family, but I no longer had that right.
lines.mao_english:
Our mother had died of illness when Akiha was born, so my sister and I were now the only Tohnos left.
Ordinarily, I───Shiki Tohno, the eldest son, would have inherited the family, but I no longer had that right.
lines.mirrorMoon:
My mother died from illness after Akiha was born, so the Tohnos had dwindled down to me and my sister.
Being the eldest son, you would think I would stand to become the Tohno heir, but I have no such privilege.
lines.mirror_moon:
My mother died from illness after Akiha was born, so the Tohnos had dwindled down to me and my sister.
Being the eldest son, you would think I would stand to become the Tohno heir, but I have no such privilege.

lines.japanese:
遠野家の跡取りになる、という事はがんじがらめの教育を受けるという事だ。
　それがイヤで自由に暮らしていて、父親から何度小言を言われたかわからない。
　そんな折、俺は事故に巻き込まれて病弱な体になってしまい、父親はこれ幸いにと俺を切り捨てた。
　父親曰く『たとえ長男であろうと、いつ死ぬかわからない者を後継者にはできん』とかなんとか。
　あいにく父親の予想を裏切って回復してしまったけれど、その頃には遠野家の跡取りは妹の秋葉に決められていた。
lines.label: s201
lines.maoEnglish:
Becoming the Tohno heir meant submitting to an education that bound you hand and foot.
I hated that and lived as freely as I could, earning more lectures from my father than I could count.
Then I was caught in the accident and left sickly, and my father seized the opportunity to cast me aside. His explanation was something like, “Eldest son or not, I cannot make an heir of someone who might die at any moment.”
Unfortunately for him, I recovered, but by then my sister Akiha had been chosen to inherit the Tohno family.
lines.mao_english:
Becoming the Tohno heir meant submitting to an education that bound you hand and foot.
I hated that and lived as freely as I could, earning more lectures from my father than I could count.
Then I was caught in the accident and left sickly, and my father seized the opportunity to cast me aside. His explanation was something like, “Eldest son or not, I cannot make an heir of someone who might die at any moment.”
Unfortunately for him, I recovered, but by then my sister Akiha had been chosen to inherit the Tohno family.
lines.mirrorMoon:
To become the Tohno heir means being bound by a strict upbringing.
I have lost count of the number of times my father had scolded me over my dislike of not being able to live freely.
That was when I got involved in that accident, and my body became weakened… My father saw it as a good opportunity to get rid of me.
His reasoning was something along the lines of "someone who could die any moment can't become the heir, even if he is the eldest son".
Sadly for my father, I betrayed his expectations by making a recovery, but my sister Akiha was already deemed to be the heir to the Tohno household.
lines.mirror_moon:
To become the Tohno heir means being bound by a strict upbringing.
I have lost count of the number of times my father had scolded me over my dislike of not being able to live freely.

lines.japanese:
それまで遠野の娘に相応しいように、と厳格に育てられていた秋葉は、それからよけい厳しく育てられたらしい。
　昔───事故に巻き込まれるまでは一緒に屋敷の庭で遊んだ秋葉とは、あれからまったく会っていない。
lines.label: s201
lines.maoEnglish:
Akiha had already been raised under strict discipline to make her a proper daughter of the Tohno family; after that, I heard, her upbringing became harsher still.
Long ago───before the accident, Akiha and I had played together in the estate gardens, but I had not seen her once in the eight years since.
lines.mao_english:
Akiha had already been raised under strict discipline to make her a proper daughter of the Tohno family; after that, I heard, her upbringing became harsher still.
Long ago───before the accident, Akiha and I had played together in the estate gardens, but I had not seen her once in the eight years since.
lines.mirrorMoon:
And so I've heard that Akiha, who was already being raised harshly in order to become a proper daughter of the Tohno household, received an even harsher upbringing since then.
That was a long time ago---I played together with Akiha in the mansion back before the accident.
After that, I never saw her again.
lines.mirror_moon:
And so I've heard that Akiha, who was already being raised harshly in order to become a proper daughter of the Tohno household, received an even harsher upbringing since then.
That was a long time ago---I played together with Akiha in the mansion back before the accident.
After that, I never saw her again.

lines.japanese:
……八年前に棄てた屋敷の生活。
　八年間という歳月は長くて、あの頃の記憶は大部分が薄れてしまっている。
　それでも。
　ある事柄だけは、今でも強く心に焼き付いている。
　それは―――――
lines.label: s201
lines.maoEnglish:
The life at the estate I abandoned eight years ago.
Eight years is a long time, and most of my memories from then had faded.
Even so.
One thing remained seared into my heart.
It was―――――
lines.mao_english:
The life at the estate I abandoned eight years ago.
Eight years is a long time, and most of my memories from then had faded.
Even so.
One thing remained seared into my heart.
It was―――――
lines.mirrorMoon:
…… The life in the mansion I abandoned eight years ago.
Those eight years were long, and my memories of that time have largely faded.
But in spite of that, there is one thing that even now continues to burn strongly within my heart, and that is-----
lines.mirror_moon:
…… The life in the mansion I abandoned eight years ago.
Those eight years were long, and my memories of that time have largely faded.
But in spite of that, there is one thing that even now continues to burn strongly within my heart, and that is-----

lines.japanese:
……まったく会っていないっていえば、それは秋葉だけの話じゃない。
　なにぶん八年前の事だからよく覚えていないけど、屋敷には同い年ぐらいの子供たちがいたはずだ。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
Akiha wasn’t the only one I hadn’t seen in all that time.
It had been eight years, so my memory was vague, but there had been other children around my age at the estate.
lines.mao_english:
Akiha wasn’t the only one I hadn’t seen in all that time.
It had been eight years, so my memory was vague, but there had been other children around my age at the estate.
lines.mirrorMoon:
…… Akiha isn't the only person I haven't seen since then.
I can't remember all the details because it's been eight years, but there were other children at the mansion around the same age as me.
lines.mirror_moon:
…… Akiha isn't the only person I haven't seen since then.
I can't remember all the details because it's been eight years, but there were other children at the mansion around the same age as me.

lines.japanese:
名前までは思い出せないけど、たしか双子の女の子だった。
　身寄りがなくて、使用人として働くことを前提に引き取った、と親父は話していた。
「……おかしいな。
子供のころは三人でよく遊んだのに、名前が思い出せないなんて」
　目を閉じて思い返す。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
I couldn’t remember their names, but I thought they were twin girls.
Father had said they had no family and had been taken in on the understanding that they would work as servants.
“How strange. We played together constantly, yet I can’t remember their names.”
I closed my eyes and searched my memory.
lines.mao_english:
I couldn’t remember their names, but I thought they were twin girls.
Father had said they had no family and had been taken in on the understanding that they would work as servants.
“How strange. We played together constantly, yet I can’t remember their names.”
I closed my eyes and searched my memory.
lines.mirrorMoon:
I don't remember their names, but there were two girls who were twins.
The old man once said that they didn't have any relatives, so he took them to work as servants.
"…… That's weird.
We played together so often when we were small, but I can't remember their names."
I close my eyes and cast my mind back.
lines.mirror_moon:
I don't remember their names, but there were two girls who were twins.
The old man once said that they didn't have any relatives, so he took them to work as servants.
"…… That's weird.
We played together so often when we were small, but I can't remember their names."
I close my eyes and cast my mind back.

lines.japanese:
たしかに思い出せる。
　いつも明るくて、見ているだけでこっちまで元気になってくるような女の子だった。
　屈託のない性格で、屋敷のみんなから可愛がられていた女の子。
　歳が近いっていう事もあって、俺とこの子はすごく気が合って、毎日のように庭を走りまわっていた。
『志貴ちゃん、いっしょにあそぼ』
　なんて言って、部屋に閉じこもっていた自分を外に連れ出してくれたのを、覚えている。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
Yes, I could remember one of them clearly.
She was always cheerful; simply looking at her filled me with energy.
Everyone at the estate adored her for her bright, untroubled nature.
We were close in age and got along wonderfully, racing through the gardens together almost every day.
‘Shiki, come play with me’
she would say, drawing me outside whenever I shut myself in my room.
lines.mao_english:
Yes, I could remember one of them clearly.
She was always cheerful; simply looking at her filled me with energy.
Everyone at the estate adored her for her bright, untroubled nature.

‘Shiki, come play with me’
she would say, drawing me outside whenever I shut myself in my room.
lines.mirrorMoon:
I should be able to remember.
She was a girl who was always cheerful, so cheerful that you would become cheerful just by looking at her.
A girl with a carefree personality who was loved by everyone at the mansion.
Because she was close to my age, I got along very well with her, and it seemed like every day we would run around the garden together.
"Let's play together, Shiki-chan."
She would say, and I could remember her taking me out of my room after I secluded myself inside.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
彼女はよく笑って、内気だった秋葉の手をとって俺たちと遊ばせようとしていた。
　もしかしすると、実際は俺たちより年上だったのかもしれない。
　あの子は俺たちや秋葉が遊ぶように手を取らせる半面、いざ俺たちが遊びだすと少し離れて俺たちの様子を見守っていてくれた。
　秋葉の教育係だった厳しい執事も仕方なさそうに『―――が一緒ならかまいません』なんて言って、秋葉を外に出してくれたことがある。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
She laughed often and would take shy little Akiha by the hand to bring her into our games.
Perhaps she had actually been older than the rest of us.
She would gather us together and make sure Akiha joined in, but once we began playing, she stepped back a little and watched over us.
Even the stern steward responsible for Akiha’s education once relented and said, ‘As long as ――― is with you, I suppose it is all right,’ before allowing Akiha outside.
lines.mao_english:
She laughed often and would take shy little Akiha by the hand to bring her into our games.

She would gather us together and make sure Akiha joined in, but once we began playing, she stepped back a little and watched over us.
Even the stern steward responsible for Akiha’s education once relented and said, ‘As long as ――― is with you, I suppose it is all right,’ before allowing Akiha outside.
lines.mirrorMoon:
She would often laugh and take shy Akiha's hand, trying to make her play with us.
Maybe she was older than the both of us.
She would guide me and Akiha to play together, but once we started playing, she would just watch over us.
Even Akiha's tutor, the harsh butler, would say "I don't mind, as long as ****** is with you guys", and let Akiha out to play.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese: だが、そんな彼女以上に気になっていた女の子がいた。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish: Yet there was another girl who occupied my thoughts even more.
lines.mao_english: Yet there was another girl who occupied my thoughts even more.
lines.mirrorMoon: But I'm much more concerned about the other girl.
lines.mirror_moon: But I'm much more concerned about the other girl.

lines.japanese:
……その子がどんな子で、どうしていつもそうしていたかは知らない。
　屋敷の二階。
　俺たちが中庭で遊んでいる時、屋敷のほうに振り返るときまって俺たちを見下ろしている少女の姿があった。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
I knew nothing about what sort of girl she was or why she always did it.
The second floor of the estate.
Whenever we played in the courtyard and I glanced back at the house, a girl was invariably standing there, looking down at us.
lines.mao_english:
I knew nothing about what sort of girl she was or why she always did it.
The second floor of the estate.
Whenever we played in the courtyard and I glanced back at the house, a girl was invariably standing there, looking down at us.
lines.mirrorMoon:
…… I don't know what kind of girl she was or why she was always like that.
From the second floor,
there was always a girl looking down at us every time I turned to look at the mansion while we were playing in the garden.
lines.mirror_moon:
…… I don't know what kind of girl she was or why she was always like that.
From the second floor,
there was always a girl looking down at us every time I turned to look at the mansion while we were playing in the garden.

lines.japanese:
あの明るい女の子と双子である少女は、けれどいつも無表情で俺たちを眺めていた。
　少女は、決して屋敷から外に出ようとはしなかった。
　ただ冷たい目をして、ずっと俺たちのことを眺めているだけ。
　……幼いながらもその少女が寂しそうだとずっと気に病んでいたのか、遠野の屋敷にいたころの思い出は彼女のことばかりだ。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
She was the cheerful girl’s twin, yet she always watched us without expression.
She never once tried to leave the estate.
She merely stood there, gazing down at us with cold eyes.
Perhaps even as a child I sensed her loneliness and could not stop worrying about her; whatever the reason, my memories of the Tohno estate were filled with that girl.
lines.mao_english:
She was the cheerful girl’s twin, yet she always watched us without expression.
She never once tried to leave the estate.
She merely stood there, gazing down at us with cold eyes.
Perhaps even as a child I sensed her loneliness and could not stop worrying about her; whatever the reason, my memories of the Tohno estate were filled with that girl.
lines.mirrorMoon:
She was the twin of that cheerful girl, but she would always gaze at us expressionlessly.
That girl would never try to leave the house.
All she would do was watch us with those cold eyes.
…… Was it because it bothered me so much that I thought she seemed so lonely?
Most of the memories I have about the Tohno mansion are only about her.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
―――まあ、結局。
　その少女とは、最後に少しだけ言葉を交わしただけだったのだが。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
―――Well, in the end.
I exchanged only a few words with that girl, just before I left.
lines.mao_english:
―――Well, in the end.
I exchanged only a few words with that girl, just before I left.
lines.mirrorMoon: ---Well, in the end, I only ended up talking a little with her.
lines.mirror_moon: ---Well, in the end, I only ended up talking a little with her.

lines.japanese:
「あの子たち、今も屋敷にいるのかな……」
　そんな事を思いだしつつ、鞄から白いリボンを取り出す。
　古びた白いリボン。
　最後に、彼女たちから渡されたもの。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
“I wonder if those girls are still at the estate…”
As the memories returned, I took a white ribbon from my bag.
An old white ribbon.
Something the girls had given me at the very end.
lines.mao_english:

An old white ribbon.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"I wonder if those girls are still at the mansion……"
While I think about that, I take a white ribbon out of my bag.
An old white ribbon that the girls gave me at the very end.
lines.mirror_moon:
"I wonder if those girls are still at the mansion……"
While I think about that, I take a white ribbon out of my bag.
An old white ribbon that the girls gave me at the very end.

lines.japanese:
―――八年前。
　事故に巻きこまれた後、遠野の屋敷から有間の家に預けられる事になった日。
　屋敷を出ようとした直前、何を思ったのか女の子はこのリボンを渡してくれた。
　……貸してあげるから、返してね。
　たしかそんなふうな事を言って、女の子は走り去っていった。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
―――Eight years ago.
After the accident, on the day I was to be sent from the Tohno estate to the Arimas.
Just before I left, for some reason, one of the girls handed me this ribbon.
I’ll lend it to you, so make sure you give it back.
She had said something like that, then run away.

lines.mirrorMoon:
---Eight years ago.

The day I was entrusted to the Arima family.
Right before I was to leave the mansion, the girl gave me this for some reason.
…… I'm just lending it to you, so be sure to return it.
Saying something along those lines, she ran off.

lines.japanese:
約束を交わした大きな木。
　その日はとてもいい天気で、見上げれば自分が消え去ってしまいそうなぐらい、高い高い青空だった。
　それが八年前、遠野の屋敷を後にする時の最後の記憶。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
The great tree where we made our promise.
The weather had been beautiful that day, and when I looked up, the blue sky seemed so high and deep that I might vanish into it.
That was my final memory of leaving the Tohno estate eight years ago.
lines.mao_english:
The great tree where we made our promise.

That was my final memory of leaving the Tohno estate eight years ago.
lines.mirrorMoon:
A promise made under a large tree.
The weather was beautiful that day.
Looking up, there was a high, high blue sky I could just lose myself in.
It was my last memory of when I left the Tohno mansion, eight years ago.
lines.mirror_moon:
A promise made under a large tree.
The weather was beautiful that day.
Looking up, there was a high, high blue sky I could just lose myself in.

lines.japanese:
「……………はあ」
　ため息をついて、リボンを鞄の中にしまう。
「けど、八年も前の話だもんなあ……」
　あの女の子がまだ屋敷にいるのかどうかも分からなければ、名前さえ覚えていない。
「……それでも、このリボンは大切な物なんだよな……」
　父である遠野槙久から勘当された当時。
　捨てられたのだという自分の立場を悲しむより、あの少女がリボンを返しに行く自分を待っていてくれると思うだけで、どこか心が温かになってくれた。
　だから、覚えているかぎりは守りたい。
　こうして屋敷に戻ることを承諾したのは秋葉が一人きりで屋敷にいるからだ。
　八年間もアイツを放っておいて、全ての責任をあいつに押しつけて勝手気侭に暮らしていた自分に負い目があるから屋敷に戻る。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
“Haaah…”
I sighed and put the ribbon back in my bag.
“But that was eight years ago…”
I did not know whether the girl was still at the estate or even remember her name.
“Even so, this ribbon matters to me.”
When my father, Makihisa Tohno, disowned me.
Rather than mourn the fact that I had been cast away, imagining that girl waiting for me to return the ribbon made me feel warm inside.
So, as long as I remembered, I wanted to keep the promise.
I had agreed to return because Akiha was alone at the estate.
I was going back because I felt guilty for abandoning her for eight years, burdening her with every responsibility while I lived however I pleased.

lines.mirrorMoon:
*sigh*
I put the ribbon back in my bag.
"But it's been eight years, after all……"
Not only do I not know if they are still at the mansion, I can't even remember their names.
"…… Even so, this ribbon is precious to me……"
The time when my father had disinherited me.
Rather than being saddened over having been discarded by him, I felt a warmness inside when I thought she was waiting for me to return the ribbon.
That's why I want to keep the promise, as long as I still remember it.
I agreed to return to the mansion because Akiha is now there all by herself.
I left her there for eight years, pushing all responsibility onto her while I selfishly lived freely.

……だが、それとは別の意味で、自分はあの約束の為に屋敷に帰るのだと思う。
　白いリボン。
　……八年前、ただ一人“待っている”と言ってくれた約束の為に。
lines.label: s202
lines.maoEnglish:
Yet apart from all that, I thought I was also returning for the sake of that promise.
The white ribbon.
For the promise made eight years ago by the only person who had told me, ‘I’ll be waiting.’
lines.mao_english:
Yet apart from all that, I thought I was also returning for the sake of that promise.
The white ribbon.
For the promise made eight years ago by the only person who had told me, ‘I’ll be waiting.’
lines.mirrorMoon:
…… But there is something else.
I really think I decided to return because of that promise.
The white ribbon.
…… Because of that promise made to the only one who said she would be waiting for me.
lines.mirror_moon:
…… But there is something else.

lines.japanese:
いつもより何分か余裕をもって教室に到着した。
「―――ふう」
　軽く深呼吸をして、窓際にある自分の机へと歩いていく。
　と。
「おはよう遠野くん」
　なんて、聞きなれない声で挨拶をされてしまった。
「―――え？」
　戸惑いながら振りかえる。
「遠野くん、さっき先生が捜してたよ。
なんかお家のことで話があるとか言ってたけど」
lines.label: s21
lines.maoEnglish:

After a small, steadying breath, I walked toward my desk beside the window.
Then.
“Good morning, Tohno.”
An unfamiliar voice greeted me.
“―――Huh?”
I turned around in confusion.
“Our teacher was looking for you earlier. He said he needed to talk about something concerning your home.”

「……ふうん。
家の事って、引っ越しについてかな」
　……住所移転の手続きは昨日すませたはずだけど、なにか不備でもあったんだろうか。

　クラスメイトの女生徒は立ち去るわけでもなく、じっとこっちの顔を見つめてくる。
「えっと……おはよう、弓塚」
「うん、おはよう遠野くん。
わたしの名前、ちゃんと覚えていてくれたんだね」
　ホッとしたように吐息をもらして、彼女―――弓塚さつきは淡く微笑んだ。
lines.label: s21
lines.maoEnglish:
“Oh. Maybe it’s about the move.”
I thought I had completed the change-of-address forms yesterday, but perhaps I had missed something.
“―――――”
The girl from my class made no move to leave; she only stood there, watching my face.
“Um—good morning, Yumizuka.”
“Good morning, Tohno. You really did remember my name.”
She let out a relieved breath, and a faint smile touched her face. Her name was Satsuki Yumizuka.

“Of course I remember my classmates’ names. We just haven’t talked much before, Yumizuka.”

lines.japanese:
ただ、弓塚さつきはクラスの中でも中心的な生徒だった。
　クラスの男子のほとんどは弓塚に熱をあげているという話だし、女子の間でも悪い噂が流れないっていう、典型的なアイドルだ。
　自然、弓塚のまわりにはいつも人だかりができてしまって、あまり社交性をもっていない俺はとは正反対の生徒だと思う。
　こっちが『弓塚さつき』という名前を覚えている事はあっても、弓塚のほうは『遠野志貴』なんていうクラスメイトの名前を覚えているはずがないんだけど、どうも今日は厄介な偶然が働いたらしい。
lines.label: s21
lines.maoEnglish:
Satsuki Yumizuka was at the heart of the class, though.
Supposedly nearly every boy had a crush on her, while not even the girls had a bad word to say. She was the quintessential popular girl.
Naturally, there was always a crowd around her. She was the complete opposite of someone as unsociable as me.
I might know the name Satsuki Yumizuka, but there was no reason she should remember an unremarkable classmate called Shiki Tohno. Yet somehow, inconveniently, she seemed to know exactly who I was.

lines.mirrorMoon:
But Yumizuka Satsuki is the center of attention.
She's often the topic of conversation among the boys, and there aren't any bad rumors about her among the girls.
In short, she's your typical class idol.
Naturally, she's always surrounded by a crowd.
She's the complete opposite of a loner like me.
While I might be able to remember the name 'Yumizuka Satsuki', there's no reason for her to remember the name 'Tohno Shiki'.
It seems like some bothersome coincidences are at work today.

「急な話だけど、もしかして転校とか、するの？」
「ああ、違う違う。
住所が変わるだけで学校は変わらないよ。
引っ越し先もこの街だし、そんなに大した事じゃないんだ」
「そう――――よかった」
　ほう、と弓塚は胸を撫で下ろす。
「……？」
　不思議だ。
どうして彼女が俺の引っ越し一つでそんなリアクションをするんだろう……？
lines.label: s21
lines.maoEnglish:
“This is sudden, but you aren’t transferring schools, are you?”
“No, nothing like that. My address is changing, but I’ll still be here. I’m only moving across town, so it’s no great upheaval.”
“Oh… Thank goodness.”
Yumizuka put a hand to her chest in relief.
“…?”
How strange. Why should a move of mine produce such a reaction from her?

lines.maoEnglish:
“Heeey, Tohno!”
A voice boomed from the classroom door without the slightest concern for who heard him.
At exactly the right moment, my friend from middle school arrived.
“Oh, it’s Yumizuka. Weird seeing you and Tohno talking.”
“…Good morning, Inui.”
Her reply was listless, and she promptly lowered her head.
Well, Yumizuka was hardly the sort who could answer cheerfully when someone like him barreled straight at her.

lines.label: s21
lines.maoEnglish:
“Picking up girls first thing in the morning—what brought this on? I thought you weren’t all that interested in girls, Tohno.”
Arihiko announced this delightful thought at the top of his lungs.
“Idiot, don’t say things that sound so bad. I’m a perfectly normal boy with a perfectly normal interest in girls.”
“Oh, good, good! Though girls these days find weird kinks more interesting than normal ones.
They’re interested, sure—nothing ever comes of it!”
Arihiko’s bottomlessly cheerful laughter rang across the early-morning classroom.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Honestly, must you be this loud first thing in the morning? I’ve got a lot on my mind and I’m already depressed, so stay away from me for the rest of the day.”
I made a shooing motion and tried to drive Arihiko off.
“Depressed? What’s wrong, Tohno? That time of the month?”
“No, I misspoke. Don’t stay away for the day; stay away for the rest of my life. Being around you seems to multiply my depression.”
Ignoring Arihiko, I went to my desk,
set down my bag, sat, and stretched with a long sigh.

Ignoring Arihiko, I went to my desk,
set down my bag, sat, and stretched with a long sigh.

じゃあさ、傷つけるなんて言わず、いっそ即死させられる方法ってないか？

「―――で、有彦。
普段は二時限目から出席する夜型人間のおまえがホームルームに顔を出すなんて、どんな風の吹き回しだ。
ちょっと、いやかなり普通じゃないぞ」
「あはは、俺だってそう思う。
たまに早起きしたからって門限守って来るもんじゃないよな、学校ってヤツは」
「……おまえの趣味には口を出さないから同意はしないよ。
俺が聞きたいのはおまえが早起きしてる理由だけだから」
「早起きの理由……？
　そうだな、最近はなにかと物騒だから夜遊びできないじゃん？
　だから必然的に夜中に眠ってしまうワケですよ。
　遠野だって知ってるだろ、ここんところ連続している通り魔事件の話」
lines.label: s21
lines.maoEnglish:
“Anyway, Arihiko. You’re a nocturnal animal who normally appears in time for second period. Seeing you at homeroom isn’t merely unusual—it’s deeply unnatural. What happened?”
“Ha ha, I was thinking the same thing. School isn’t somewhere you show up on time just because you happened to wake up early.”
“…I’m not going to tell you how to live, but don’t expect me to agree. I only asked why you were awake.”
“Why I woke up? Well, it’s dangerous out lately, so I can’t go carousing at night. That means I end up sleeping after dark like some respectable citizen.
You’ve heard about the string of random attacks, haven’t you?”

lines.japanese:
「ああ、思い出した！
　被害者全員がバラバラ死体で、アソートを作れるんだとかどうとか！」
「……違うよ、乾くん。
殺されちゃった人はみんな、体内の血液が著しく失われている、でしょう？」
「ああ、そうだったそうだった。
現代の吸血鬼かっていう見出しだったもんな、アレ」
「ふうん。
詳しいんだね、弓塚さん」
「そんなコトないよ。
この街で起きている事件なんだもん、ニュースを見てればイヤでも覚えちゃうことだと思う」
　……そうだったのか。
　たしか隣の街で起きてる事件だと思ったけど、いつのまにかこの街に移り変わっていたんだ。
lines.label: s21
lines.maoEnglish:
“Oh, I remember! They were all chopped up. Enough pieces to mix and match a whole assortment!”
“…That’s not it, Inui. Every victim had suffered severe blood loss, remember?”
“Right, right. That headline called the killer a modern-day vampire.”
“You know a lot about it, Yumizuka.”
“Not really. It’s happening in our own town. Anyone who watches the news would remember, whether they wanted to or not.”
…I hadn’t realized.
I thought the murders had been taking place in the neighboring town, but at some point they had moved into ours.

“No, I’m fine so far. I appreciate the concern, but if I were fainting every hour of every day, my body wouldn’t last long.”
“Fair point. If you say you’re all right, I suppose you are.”

二時限目の授業が終わった。
　担任でもある数学の教師は、
「遠野、書類の書き漏らしがあるそうだから事務室に行ってきなさい」
　と去り際に伝えてきた。
　すぐに済むらしいので、三時限目が始まる前に事務室に行ってしまおう。
　事務室は一階にある。
　三階である二年の教室から離れているが、ダッシュで行けば三時限目が始まるまでに戻って来れるだろう。

The office was on the first floor.
It was a long way from the second-year classrooms on the third, but if I ran, I could still make it back before the bell.

“Yes?”

“…”

“Ah—well…”
Her eyes behind the glasses were so direct they seemed capable of drawing me in.
They were so earnest that I felt almost guilty for interrupting her.
The wooden brace before her was rotten and crumbling, far beyond use.

lines.label: s22
lines.maoEnglish:
Once I joined in, the repairs proved less difficult than expected.
Though inexperienced, the girl in glasses was deft; as soon as she found the knack, she worked briskly and efficiently.
Every movement she made was crisp and energetic, so satisfying to watch that it lifted my spirits.
Before I knew it, only one brace remained.
About thirty minutes had passed.
I couldn’t stay away from class any longer, and with only one brace left, she should be fine on her own.
“Well, I should be going.”
I stood and brushed the dust from my trousers.
The girl in glasses rose as well, then stared at me with the same unbroken intensity as before.
“…?”
Come to think of it, who was she?
Her behavior had been so peculiar that the question had never occurred to me, but now that I looked calmly, I realized she was beautiful.
If there were a girl this striking in the third year, surely rumors about “that beautiful third-year who looks so good in glasses” would have spread among the boys.

If you make a carefree face like that in front of your rival, you'd better be prepared for trouble!"
In any case, Arihiko is a loud guy.
"Yo!
Morning, Tohno!"
Before I know it, everyone in class is looking my way and greeting me.

lines.japanese:
「……有彦、うるさい。
こっそり教室に入ってさりげなく次の授業を受けようっていうこっちの意向を台無しにしやがって。
　そもそもなんで俺とおまえがライバルなんだ。
ケンカに強いのなら他にいっぱいいるんだから、あんまりかまわないでくれ」
　……まあ、たしかに中学からこっち、総額一万円近い金額を貸してはいるから敵と呼べない事もないけど。
「どうしてかな、遠野ってばオレにだけ冷たいよな。
他のヤツラには聖人君子みたいなヤツなのに、不公平だ」

「なんだ、わかってるじゃないか。
世の中、公平なコトはあんまりないよ」
「……はあ。
やっぱり遠野はオレにだけ冷たいよなあ」
　大げさにため息をつく有彦。
　別段こっちとしても有彦に冷たくあたっているわけではなくて、なんというか、コイツとはこういう関係になってしまうのだ。
lines.label: s22
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Arihiko, be quiet. You’ve ruined my plan to slip in unnoticed and casually attend the next lesson.
And why are we rivals in the first place? If you want someone strong to fight, there are plenty of better candidates. Stop pestering me.”
Then again, I had lent him nearly ten thousand yen since middle school, so perhaps he qualified as an enemy after all.
“Why are you only ever cold to me, Tohno? With everyone else, you’re a saint. It’s unfair.”
“So you do understand. Very little in this world is fair.”
“…Haaah. You really are only cold to me.”
Arihiko heaved an exaggerated sigh.
It wasn’t that I deliberately treated him coldly. Somehow, this was simply what happened whenever the two of us were together.

「それより有彦。
普段は二時限目から出席する夜型人間のおまえが朝から出席してるなんて、どんな風の吹き回しだ。
ちょっと、いやかなり普通じゃないぞ」
「まあな、オレだってそう思う。
たまに早起きしたからって一時限目から来るもんじゃないよな、学校ってヤツは」
「……まあ、おまえの趣味には口を出さないよ。
俺が聞きたいのはおまえが早起きしてる理由だけだから」
「そりゃあ最近はなにかと物騒だから夜は大人しく眠るコトにしているんだよ。
遠野だって知ってるだろ、ここんところ連続している通り魔事件の話」
lines.label: s22
lines.maoEnglish:
“More importantly, Arihiko, you’re a nocturnal animal who normally appears in time for second period. Seeing you here this early isn’t merely unusual—it’s deeply unnatural. What happened?”
“Fair point. I was thinking the same thing. School isn’t someplace you come for first period just because you happened to wake up early.”
“…I’m not going to tell you how to live, so I won’t argue. I only asked why you were awake.”
“Things have been dangerous lately, so I’ve decided to behave myself and sleep at night. You’ve heard about the string of random attacks, haven’t you?”

lines.label: s22
lines.maoEnglish:
The string of random murders…?
“Oh, right. There was something like that.”
Arihiko’s words brought it back to me.
I felt mildly ashamed. For the last few days, I had been too preoccupied with whether I would return to the Tohno house to pay any attention to the news.

「ああ、思い出した！

lines.label: s22
lines.maoEnglish:
“What was that trashy headline? ‘The Grisly Serial Murders’ or something?”
“There’s more. Every victim was a young woman, and the one killed two days ago was number eight. And every last one of them was—what was it again?”
Arihiko tilted his head.
“…”
Apparently I’d been a fool to ask him.
“Oh, I remember! Every victim had an X-shaped wound across her throat.”

「ああ、そうだったそうだった。

「ふうん。
詳しいんだね、弓塚さん」
「そんなコトないよ。
この街で起きている事件なんだもん、ニュースを見てればイヤでも覚えちゃうことだと思う」
　……そうだったのか。
　たしか隣の街で起きている事件だと思ったけど、いつのまにかこの街に移り変わっていたんだ。

“That’s not it, Inui. Every victim had suffered severe blood loss.”
“Right, right. That headline called the killer a modern-day vampire.”

It’s happening in our own town. Anyone who watches the news would remember, whether they wanted to or not.”
I hadn’t realized.
I thought the murders had been taking place in the neighboring town, but at some point they had moved into ours.

「――とまあ、そういうコトだよ遠野。
　いくらオレでもね、夜中に殺人犯が出歩いているうちは夜遊びはしない。
そういうわけで最近はまじめに朝七時に目を覚ましているのだ」
「……なんだ、そんな理由だったのか。
まともすぎてつまらないな」
　有彦をあしらいながら席に座る。
「なんだよ、つれないな。
さてはアレか、朝から貧血でぶっ倒れたのか？」
「いや、今朝はまだ大丈夫。

「ああ、そりゃもっともだ。

lines.label: s22
lines.maoEnglish:
“So there you have it, Tohno.
Even I’m not going out at night while a murderer is prowling the streets. That’s why I’ve been waking up like a model citizen at seven every morning.”
“…That’s all? What a disappointingly sensible reason.”
I brushed Arihiko off and sat down.
“You’re no fun. Did you collapse from anemia again this morning?”
“No, I’m fine so far. I appreciate the concern, but if I were fainting every hour of every day, my body wouldn’t last long.”
“Fair point. If you say you’re all right, I suppose you are.”

「ほら、授業が始まるぞ。
早く席に戻れ」
「あいよ。
……っと、そうそう。
今日の昼メシな、屋上じゃなくて食堂でするからな。
本日は特別ゲストをお呼びしているので、楽しみにしているコト」
　きしし、と何か企んでいそうな笑い声をあげて、有彦は自分の席に戻っていった。
「それじゃあね、遠野くん」
「あ―――うん、弓塚さんも、付き合わせて悪かったね」
　たったった、と軽い足取りで弓塚も席に戻る。
　……しかし。
　クラスメイトというだけの彼女が、どうして俺たちの会話に入ってきたのかは謎だった。
lines.label: s22
lines.maoEnglish:
While we talked, the warning bell rang.
“There’s the bell. Get back to your seat.”
“Sure thing. Oh, right—lunch today is in the cafeteria, not on the roof. We have a special guest joining us, so look forward to it.”
With a scheming little cackle, Arihiko returned to his seat.
“See you later, Tohno.”
“Ah—right. Sorry you got dragged into all that, Yumizuka.”
Yumizuka trotted lightly back to her own seat.
…Still:
why had a girl who was merely my classmate joined our conversation at all?

lines.japanese:
教室に残る。
　ちなみに、遠野志貴の昼食は毎日気分で変動する。
　お弁当を作ってもらう事もあれば、うどんが恋しくなって学食に移動する事もあり、食事が面倒くさくなったら購買にいってパンと牛乳を買ったりもする。
　今日はお弁当は作ってもらっていない。
もう有間の家には帰らないんだから、お弁当を作ってもらうのは辞退したのだ。
　よって、こうして教室に残っていても食べるものなんて何もない。
「気は乗らないけど食堂に行くか」
　結局それか、と呆れながら教室を後にした。
lines.label: s25
lines.maoEnglish:
I stayed in the classroom.
For the record, what Shiki Tohno ate for lunch changed with his mood every day.
Some days I had a packed lunch made for me; some days I craved udon and went to the cafeteria; and when eating felt like too much bother, I bought bread and milk from the school store.
No one had packed anything for me today. Since I wouldn’t be returning to the Arima house, I had declined the offer.
So there was nothing for me to eat if I stayed here.
“I don’t much feel like it, but I suppose I’ll go to the cafeteria.”
So much for staying in the classroom, I thought as I left.

lines.maoEnglish:
“You’re late, Tohno. I told you we had a special guest today. You could’ve hurried.”
For all his complaints, Arihiko was sitting alone.
“So who is this special guest?”
“Well, she turned me down. Said she had something to do today and that we should make it another time.”
“Oh? The guest was a girl, then?”
“Yeah, an upperclassman I’ve been making moves on lately. She’s popular in all sorts of ways, so what can you do?”
With that cheerful declaration, Arihiko slurped his curry udon.
He could be relentless until the instant he gave up, and then perfectly breezy about it; that was one of his better qualities.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Arihiko, your appearance does you a serious disservice. Underneath it all, you’re a painfully sensitive and sentimental fellow.”
“Heh heh—if the perpetually melancholy Tohno says so, I suppose I must be the real thing.”
Arihiko noisily slurped up more noodles.

“Taking what?”
“You’ve lived with the Arimas since elementary school, haven’t you? I don’t know why, but it’s been eight years. Why would your father suddenly summon the son he disowned after all this time?”

“I wasn’t disowned. I was just sort of thrown out of the estate.”
“Tohno. If a family throws a child out for no particular reason, that stops being a tragedy and becomes a joke. Oh, it is party joke. But is too cold, so laugh—NO.”
Arihiko spread his hands and shrugged theatrically.
His most obvious trait was his refusal to become serious under any circumstances.
“You’re right. If I were thrown out for no reason, I guess all I could do is laugh.”

"Tohno-kun, if there ever was a family that kicked their kid out of their house 'somehow', that's not a tragedy, it's a comedy.

“Arihiko, your appearance does you a serious disservice. Underneath it all, you’re a painfully sensitive and sentimental fellow.”

lines.japanese:
「勘当されてたわけじゃないよ。
なんとなく屋敷から追い出されただけなんだ」
「遠野くん。
なんとなくで子供を家から追い出すような家庭があったら、それはすでに悲劇ではなく笑い話だ。
オー、イッツパーティージョーク。
しかし寒すぎて笑え、ナイ」
　有彦は大げさに両手を広げて肩をすくめる。
　どんな時でも深刻にならないのが有彦のわかりやすい特徴だ。
「……そうだな。
たしかになんとなくで家から追い出されたら、そりゃあ笑うしかないだろうね」
lines.label: s26
lines.maoEnglish:
“I wasn’t disowned. I was just sort of thrown out of the estate.”
“Tohno. If a family throws a child out for no particular reason, that stops being a tragedy and becomes a joke. Oh, it is party joke. But is too cold, so laugh—NO.”
Arihiko spread his hands and shrugged theatrically.
His most obvious trait was his refusal to become serious under any circumstances.
“You’re right. If I were thrown out for no reason, I guess all I could do is laugh.”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"He didn't 'disinherit' me.
He just kicked me out of the house somehow."
"Tohno-kun, if there ever was a family that kicked their kid out of their house 'somehow', that's not a tragedy, it's a comedy.
But it's so boring, it's not even funny."
Arihiko spreads his arms and shrugs.
Refusing to be serious, ever, is one of Arihiko's easy-to-understand traits.
"…… Yeah, I guess you're right.
If you get kicked out of the house, laughing is all you really can do."

　有彦はどんぶりを両手でもって、ぐびぐびと熱いカレースープを飲み干していく。

lines.label: s26
lines.maoEnglish:
“Exactly. And didn’t they give you the grand line about never darkening their doorstep again? The rest of society calls that disowning someone.
I’ve never asked before, but why did they disown you?”
“…”
I had no idea.
I would have liked an answer myself.
“Well, if you don’t want to talk about it, forget it.”
Arihiko raised his bowl in both hands and gulped down the hot curry broth.
Lunch break was short.
Following his example, I hurriedly finished my own udon.

昼休みの廊下はなにかと混みあっている。
　これから学食に行こうとする生徒や、お弁当を片手にお気に入りの場所に向かう生徒たち。
　そんな人の流れに混ざりながら、学食に行こうか購買に行こうかふらふらと迷ってみる。
「……………」

lines.maoEnglish:
The corridors were crowded at lunchtime.
Students were heading for the cafeteria or carrying boxed lunches to their favorite haunts.
I drifted with the flow, unable to decide between the cafeteria and the school store.
“…”

If I had time to loiter here, I might as well join Arihiko in the cafeteria.
I started toward the cafeteria.
On the way, someone I knew came running toward me, waving.

lines.label: s27
lines.maoEnglish:
“Thank goodness. I’ve been looking everywhere for you, Tohno.”
“Oh—Ciel. Hello.”
―――For some reason, I grew self-conscious and gave her that muddled greeting.
“Good afternoon. We’ve already seen each other today, so I suppose there’s no need to greet each other again.”

“―――Oh, right, I suppose we have.”
Growing even more embarrassed, I looked away and gave another halfhearted answer.

　ハッとして自分の口を押さえる有彦。
「……わりい。
無闇に口にするコトじゃなかった」
「いいよ。
別に悪いことじゃないんだから」
　有彦の顔を見ずに、カレーライスを食べながらそう言った。
「そっか。
ま、そーだよな。
アレで文句を言ったらバチが当たるってもんか」
　うん、と納得する有彦。
　こいつのこういう、突き抜けたような楽観性は本当にうらやましい。
lines.label: s27
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ah――――”
Arihiko caught himself and covered his mouth.
“…Sorry—that wasn’t mine to blurt out.”
“It’s fine. It isn’t anything shameful.”
Without looking at him, I kept eating my curry rice.
“Right. Yeah, of course. After all they did for you, you’d be tempting fate if you complained.”
Arihiko nodded, satisfied.
I really envied that irrepressible optimism of his.

The Arimas are the family who took him in, by the way, and they’re wonderful people—from where I stood, it was a happy home.
And yet he turned down their offer to adopt him, then ran to my place every holiday. Seriously, what are you so unhappy about?”

　……中学校から友人だった有彦ならいざ知らず、先輩を相手にこんなこみいった話をしても迷惑なだけだろう。

lines.maoEnglish:

“No, not at all. I’m the one who asked something strange—I’m sorry.”
She tried to sound bright.
Arihiko had known me since middle school, but burdening her with such complicated family business could only be awkward.
In fact, she was fidgeting as though deeply uncomfortable.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Uh, sorry, but I need to speak to Tohno in private. Would you mind giving us a minute?”
Arihiko tossed out the outrageous request as casually as anything.

“Y-you idiot! What are you saying? We can talk privately anywhere, and she’s already fin――

lines.maoEnglish:
“Sure. She’s the best-looking girl in the whole school. But if something that minor is enough to put her off me, then to hell with it.
And another thing. I really did need to speak to you in private.”
“…?”

I snapped apart my chopsticks and began on the curry udon.
“What is it? Don’t suddenly get serious; it’s creepy. And if you want money, I haven’t got any. As of today, I begin my new life as an impoverished youth.”

I see.
Apparently, in his own way, Arihiko had been worried about Shiki Tohno.

lines.label: s27
lines.maoEnglish:
“Exactly. And they even gave you the grand line about never darkening their doorstep again. The rest of society calls that disowning someone.
I’ve never asked before, but why did they disown you?”
“…”
I had no idea.
I would have liked an answer myself.
“Well, if you don’t want to talk about it, forget it.”
Arihiko raised his bowl in both hands and gulped down the cold mochi-udon broth.
Lunch break was short.
Following his example, I hurriedly finished my own curry udon.

“Exactly. And they even gave you the grand line about never darkening their doorstep again. The rest of society calls that disowning someone.
I’ve never asked before, but why did they disown you?”
“…”
I had no idea.
I would have liked an answer myself.
“Well, if you don’t want to talk about it, forget it.”
Arihiko raised his bowl in both hands and gulped down the cold udon broth.
Lunch break was short.
Following his example, I hurriedly finished my own mochi udon.

Lunchtime is short.

lines.japanese:
食堂の席は、もうほとんどが埋まっていた。
　教室でぼんやりとしていたタイムロスのせいで、学食の席はほぼ全滅状態になっている。
「―――空いてる席なんてない、か」
　混雑した学食を見渡す。
　この時間で席なんて空いているはずがないけど、それでも一応テーブルの状態を確認する。
「………あ」
　驚いた、というより呆れた。
　ものの見事に二つといわず三つも四つも席が空いているテーブルがある。
lines.label: s29
lines.maoEnglish:
Almost every seat in the cafeteria was already taken.
Thanks to the time I had wasted staring into space in the classroom, nearly every seat was gone.
“―――No seats left, then.”
I surveyed the packed cafeteria.
Nothing should have been free at this hour, but I checked the tables anyway.
“Oh.”
I was less surprised than exasperated.
One table had not two but three or four empty seats.

lines.mirrorMoon:
Almost all the seats in the cafeteria are taken.
Because I spaced out in the hallway, empty seats are pretty much non-existent at this point.
"---Aren't there any empty seats?"
I cast my gaze over the crowded cafeteria.
There shouldn't be any spare seats this late, but I decide to check the tables out anyway.

"…… Ah."
I'm surprised…… no, I'm astounded.
There, plain as day, is a table with not two, not even three, but four unoccupied seats.
There are two students sitting at the table, and it seems like one of them noticed me during my efforts to locate a seat.

そこに座っている生徒は二人。
　そのうちの一人が、席を探してきょろきょろしている俺に気がついたみたいだ。
「いょぉう、遠野！」

　あたま、いたい。

Two students sat there.
One of them seemed to notice me looking around.
“Heeey, Tohno!”
The student waving both arms was my orange-haired classmate.
“…”
My head hurt.
But there were no other empty seats, so I reluctantly headed for my waving friend’s table.

lines.label: s29
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hey, Tohno―――wait, what? You know him?”
“Yes, we’ve already met once today. We ran smack into each other in the corridor, didn’t we, Tohno?”
“Ah—yes, sorry about that.”
I bowed my head in apology.
“No, I’m sorry; I was daydreaming. You’re very conscientious, Tohno.”
“Conscientious—hardly,” I began, but she only smiled and nodded with evident satisfaction.
There really was something singular about her.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Come on, sit down, my dearest friend! If you stand there gawping any longer, your precious mochi udon will get soggy. Now sit and tell me every last detail of how you met Ciel without my permission.”

Arihiko seemed close to Ciel.
Unlike me, who had met her only a handful of times, he spoke to her with easy familiarity.
“By the way, you said you collided with Tohno earlier—what happened?”

“Huh. I can’t imagine Tohno making a blunder like that. He may look half asleep, but underneath he’s incredibly dependable; I guess he’s bad at leaning on people and hates causing anyone trouble.”

lines.maoEnglish:
“Ciel, I’m not transferring. I’m only changing where I live today, so I had to submit a change-of-address form.”
“Then you’re going to live alone?”
“That’s not it either. I’m only returning to my own home.
It’s that absurdly grand place on top of the hill, so the whole thing still doesn’t feel real.”
“I see. Could that be the Tohno estate?”
Ciel asked timidly, as though afraid of prying.
To the people of this town, the Tohno family’s Western-style house on the hill must have seemed like something apart.
I hadn’t returned for eight years myself, but in my memory the Tohno estate was absurdly large.
“That’s right. I know I’ll be out of place there, but the move is already settled, so there’s no use arguing.”
“───Huh. From the sound of it, you weren’t too excited about going back.”
“Honestly, I feel neither good nor bad about it. I’m not sure what I feel myself.”
“Well, even if it’s your home, you haven’t been there in eight years. No wonder you’re uneasy. It’ll probably feel like somebody else’s house for a while.”

Arihiko spreads his arms and shrugs.
"…… Yeah, I guess you're right.
If you get kicked out of the house, all you can really do is laugh."

lines.japanese:
「だろう？
　おまけに二度と敷居は跨ぐなっていう決め台詞付きときた。
世間さまではそーゆーのは勘当というんだぞ。
　今まで聞かなかったけどな、おまえはどうして勘当されたんだ」
「……………」
　……………さあ。
　そんな事、こっちが聞きたいぐらいだ。
「ま、話したくないなら、いい」
　有彦はどんぶりを両手でもって、ぐびぐびと冷めたうどんの汁を飲み干していく。
　休み時間は短い。
　有彦の早食いを見習って、こっちもぐびぐびと力うどんを平らげる事にした。
lines.label: s29
lines.maoEnglish:
“Exactly. And they even gave you the grand line about never darkening their doorstep again. The rest of society calls that disowning someone.
I’ve never asked before, but why did they disown you?”
“…”
I had no idea.
I would have liked an answer myself.
“Well, if you don’t want to talk about it, forget it.”
Arihiko raised his bowl in both hands and gulped down the cold udon broth.
Lunch break was short.
Following his example, I hurriedly finished my own mochi udon.
