lines.japanese:
昼休みになって、教室は騒々と活性化する。
　食堂に向かって飛び出していく男子、机をくっつけてテーブルを作る女子のグループ、弁当を手にしてゆったりと教室を出ていく生徒。
　そんな光景を眺めながら、自分の机に購買で買ってきた三角パンと牛乳を置く。
「ったく、相変わらず小食だな遠野は」
　……目の前にこの男がいるのは、もはや日常なのでいまさら文句を言っても始まらない。
lines.label: s30
lines.maoEnglish:
At lunchtime, the classroom came noisily to life.
Boys raced for the cafeteria; groups of girls pushed their desks together into tables; students with boxed lunches drifted leisurely out of the room.
Watching it all, I set a triangular bun and a carton of milk from the school store on my desk.
“Honestly, Tohno, you still eat like a bird.”
Arihiko’s presence opposite me had become so routine that there was no point complaining anymore.

lines.mirrorMoon:
It's lunchtime and the classroom starts to liven up.
Some guys are dashing off towards the cafeteria, a group of girls are rearranging desks to form a table, and some students are calmly leaving the classroom, boxed lunches in hand.
I watch them while I set down the milk and bread I bought.
"Sheesh, not much of an appetite as usual, huh, Tohno?"
This guy in front of me being here is already a part of my daily routine, and I'm not about to start complaining now.

食事に華がないのはどうかと思うんよ、オレ」
「そう。
華がないならあっちのグループに入れてもらえば？
　別に止めないよ、俺は」
「ばかもの、華っていうのは可憐なのが一輪咲いているからいいんじゃねえか。
ああゆうふうに徒党をくんでるのは駄目だね。
美しくないどころかありふれて毒に見える」
　……女子のグループに聞かれていたら石でも投げられかねない発言をする有彦。
　幸い、今のところコイツの毒舌がクラスの女子に聞かれたコトはない。
lines.label: s30
lines.maoEnglish:
“Still, there’s something bleak about two grown men sitting face-to-face over lunch. This table needs a little feminine grace.”
“Right. Then ask that group to let you join them. I won’t stop you.”
“Fool. Grace is one delicate flower blooming alone. A whole huddle like that is no good—it’s not beautiful; it’s so commonplace it looks poisonous.”
Arihiko made a remark that might have gotten him pelted with stones if the girls had heard.
Fortunately, none of the girls in class had heard his venomous remarks yet.

lines.label: s30
lines.maoEnglish:
“That’s vicious, Arihiko. You’ve always been awful, but haven’t you gotten even worse lately? You’ve crossed from awful into godawful.”
“Can’t be helped. There’s a genuinely beautiful flower at this school, so naturally my standards have risen.”
“…Who is this beautiful flower?”
“That’s a secret. I’d rather not create more rivals.”
Arihiko chuckled, his smile nakedly ambitious.
I almost admired how openly he displayed something I seemed to lack.

lines.label: s30
lines.maoEnglish:
――――And then.
Someone I had met only a little while ago came through the classroom door and headed toward us.
“Oh.”
Carrying a boxed lunch, the approaching figure was impossible to mistake―――
“Hello, Tohno. I came to join you for lunch—is that all right?”
“Wh―――oh, of course, but―――”
Still smiling, Ciel fetched a chair and sat down as if it were the most natural thing in the world.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Ciel, were you hurt after all?”
“No, I wasn’t hurt at all, though.”
That answer, delivered with a smile, left me at a loss.
“You told me to come by at lunch, so I thought I ought to.”
“Well—I did say that.”
What I had meant was that she should come if she discovered an injury, so I could take responsibility.

“Yes, I know. The Arimas head some school of tea ceremony, don’t they? So they’re strict with you too.”

“I see—but how did you know I lived with the Arimas? I haven’t told anyone since we started high school.”

「遠野。

「やめとけって、なんで」

　有彦は自分の席に戻っていく。

lines.label: s30
lines.maoEnglish:
“Tohno. Stay away from Yumizuka.”
The words came quietly.
Arihiko’s face was more serious than I had ever seen it.
“Why should I stay away from her?”
“Yeah. Yumizuka may not look it, but she’s shy and utterly devoted. She’s a terrible match for an oblivious idiot like you. Girls like her are dangerous once things get serious.”
Arihiko went back to his desk.
“What’s he talking about? It’s not as if I’m trying to start anything with Yumizuka.”
I muttered it to no one in particular and dropped into my chair.

lines.japanese:
一日の授業がすべて終わって、放課後になった。
　すぐさま屋敷に帰る気になれず、ぼんやりと窓越しに校庭を眺める。
　教室は夕焼けのオレンジ色で染め上げられている。
　水彩の赤絵の具に濡れたような色をしていて、目に痛い。
　……朱色は苦手だ。
　眼球の奥に染み込んできそうで、吐き気がする。

lines.maoEnglish:
Classes ended, and the school day was over.
I couldn’t bring myself to return to the estate at once.
The classroom glowed orange in the sunset.
It was the color of wet red watercolor, so vivid it hurt my eyes.
I hated scarlet.
It made me sick, as though the color might seep in behind my eyes.

lines.japanese:
どうも、自分は血を連想させる物に弱い体質であるらしい。
　いや、正確には血に弱い体質になってしまった、というべきかもしれない。
　八年前、遠野志貴は死ぬような目にあったという。
　それはものすごい大事故で、偶然いあわせた自分は胸に傷をおってしまい、何日か生死の境をさまよったとの事だ。
　本来なら即死していてもおかしくない傷だったらしいのだけど、医師の対応がよかったのか奇跡的に命を取り留めたという。
　当人である俺自身は、その時の傷があんまりにも重すぎてよく覚えてはいない。
lines.label: s31
lines.maoEnglish:
Anything that called blood to mind seemed to disagree with me.
Or perhaps it would be more accurate to say that blood had begun to disagree with me after the accident.
Eight years ago, Shiki Tohno nearly died—or so I had been told.
It was a terrible accident; I happened to be there, suffered a wound to the chest, and spent several days between life and death.
The wound should have killed me instantly, but through either the doctors’ skill or sheer luck, I survived.
I was the one it happened to, yet the injury was so grave that I remembered almost nothing.

lines.mirrorMoon:
It seems I am weak against things that resemble blood.
No, I should say I am weak against blood itself.
Eight years ago, I had a near-death experience.
I was in an accident where I was injured in the chest and I teetered between life and death for days.
I should've died instantly.
But, miraculously, I survived.
Maybe it's because of the great medical treatment.
However, the injuries were so severe that I don't even remember the accident.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: The source conspicuously reports that 'Tohno Shiki is said to have nearly died,' continues with hearsay about the accident, and only then returns to the first-person sufferer who cannot remember it. mirror moon recasts the passage as a straightforward autobiographical memory, erasing the distance between Shiki, his name, and the account he has been told.

　事故のことはよく覚えてないけれど、今でも胸にはその時の傷跡が残っている。
　なんでもガラスの破片が体に突きささってしまったとかで、胸の真ん中と背中には火傷の跡のような傷がある。

lines.maoEnglish:
Eight years ago, when I was a child.
Something suddenly punched straight through the center of my chest, and I lost consciousness.
After that, I remembered only pain and cold until I woke in a hospital bed.
I remember little of the accident, but it left its scars on me.
They say a shard of glass was driven into my body; to this day, I have marks like burns in the center of my chest and across my back.

“The scar on my chest.”
A great scar in the center of my chest, hidden beneath my uniform.

lines.label: s31
lines.maoEnglish:
Come to think of it, that accident was also when I began seeing those “lines.”
Now the glasses Teach gave me let me shut them out and forget they exist, but without her, I think my mind would have broken long ago.
Keiko had been my mother until that day―――and as we parted, she told me there was something wrong with the Tohno estate.
“Nothing to worry about, then. I’m hardly normal myself.”
I pushed my slipping glasses back into place and picked up my bag.
I couldn’t remain in the classroom forever.

lines.label: s33
lines.maoEnglish:
“Are you free, Tohno?”
“Well ─── if having nothing to do counts as being free, then I unquestionably am.”
She caught my sleeve and gave it a little tug.
“Then I’ve caught you. Come have tea with me.”
Her invitation came with a smile.
I had no reason to refuse—and talking with her might actually be rather nice.

もしかして茶道部か何かの部室？」
「はい、一応茶道部の部室ってことになってます。
わたしが入るまでは使われてなかったみたいですけど」
　先輩は先に畳の上にあがっていくと、なにやらガチャガチャと用意をしはじめた。
「部室かぁ……でも先輩、それだと他の部員さんたちがやってくるんじゃないか？

「だいじょうぶ、茶道部っていっても部員はわたししかいませんから。
そのおかげで放課後とか休み時間とか、こんなふうに自由に使っちゃってるわけなんです、はい」
　笑いながら先輩はざぶとんを敷いてくれた。
　お茶はお茶でも、本当に真面目なお茶会らしい。

lines.label: s33
lines.maoEnglish:
“Oh. I never knew our school had a room like this. Is it the tea club’s room?”
“Yes, officially. It seems no one used it before I joined.”
She stepped onto the tatami ahead of me and began clattering through her preparations.
“A clubroom—but won’t the other members be coming? It can’t be good to have an outsider like me in here.”
“Don’t worry. The tea club may have a room, but I’m its only member, so I can use it however I please after school or during breaks.”
Laughing, she laid out a floor cushion for me.
So when she said tea, she meant an honest-to-goodness tea gathering.
Frankly, this kind of thing put me out of my depth.

lines.label: s33
lines.maoEnglish:
“Listen, Ciel. I haven’t the faintest idea what the proper etiquette is.”
“What are you talking about? I only know the casual procedure myself.”
She answered without hesitation and came over carrying a tray with a teapot, cups, and sweets.
“We’re only here to chat, so let’s forget all the stiff formalities. They take all the fun out of it.”
She smiled gently and poured tea into her cup.

lines.mirrorMoon:

"We are just going to have a casual conversation, so there's no need to be so formal.

lines.maoEnglish:
“…I really don’t understand you, Ciel.”
Grumbling, I poured my own tea.
I noisily sipped my tea.
I ate one of the bean-paste wafers she had served, then drank again.
I had never involved myself in it, but the Arima family headed a school of tea ceremony.
Perhaps growing up in that house had made me accustomed to sitting idly in a tatami room over tea.
Ciel was watching me with a strangely troubled expression.

“Then the Arimas have effectively been your parents since you were nine?”

That was how I brought the story to a close.
Ciel gave a tiny, silent nod.

And I thought there was something good in being able to trust such blind, unquestioning affection.”
───These people love me.
So I have to hurry,
As soon as I can, I have to become a real member of their family───
lines.mirrorMoon:
"No, I liked them.
They were people who didn't care that I wasn't related to them by blood.
They were so warm to me that I felt bad about being depressed all by myself.
And for them to love me no matter what…… I didn't think it was a bad thing."

---I was loved by these people.
That's why soon, even one day sooner,
I have to truly become family to them---

evidence.japanese:
「いや、好きだったな。
血が繋がってないことなんて気にも留めない人たちで、俺が一人で落ち込んでいるのが申し訳なくなってくるぐらい、温かかった。
　そういう盲目的な愛情を信じられる自分っていうのも、悪くないと思ってた」
 ───この人たちは自分を愛してくれている。
　　　だから早く、一日でも早く、
　　　ボクは本当の家族にならなくちゃ───

lines.maoEnglish:
I had repeated those words to myself ever since I was small.
Ever since a time so long ago it scarcely felt real.
Again and again, until the years made me dizzy, I had sworn the same vow───

…… Since a very, very long time ago.
Over and over, I swore, till I would practically pass out.

lines.japanese:
「……えっと、たしかに有彦のいうとおり、有間の家に不満なんかひとつもなかったんです。
　あの人たちは良くしてくれたし、自分もその愛情に応えてきたと思う。
　そりゃあお互い、こんなのは家族ごっこだってわかってたけど、芝居じみたそれでさえ、苦痛ではなかったから」
　いや、むしろ幸せだっただろう。
　ある意味。
有間の両親と俺は、理想の親子だったと思う。
lines.label: s34
lines.maoEnglish:
“Arihiko was right—I didn’t resent a single thing about living with the Arimas.
They treated me well, and I think I returned their affection.
Of course we both knew we were playing at being a family, but even that little performance never caused me pain.”
No—if anything, I had been happy.
In one sense, at least. I think the Arimas and I had the ideal parent-child relationship.

lines.japanese:
「───でも、だめだったんですね」
「……ああ。
それでも、一線をこえられなかった。
自分は本当の家族じゃない、という言葉がどうしても頭から離れてくれなくてね。
　そんなこと無視するべきだとわかってんだけど、どうしてもダメなんだ。
　幼児体験だかなんだかしらないけど、こうなるとすでに呪いだね。
なんだか、どこにいっても家族とはずっと他人のような気がする」
　先輩は黙っている。
　視線をそらして、申し訳なさそうに肩をすぼめていた。
lines.label: s34
lines.maoEnglish:
“───But it still wasn’t enough.”
“No—I could never cross that final boundary. I couldn’t drive the words ‘you aren’t truly family’ out of my head. I knew I ought to ignore them, but I simply couldn’t.
Maybe it comes from something that happened when I was little; I don’t know.
At this point it feels like a curse. Wherever I went, I felt as though my family and I would always be strangers.”
She said nothing.
She looked away and hunched her shoulders as if apologizing.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"---But it was no good, was it?"
"…… Yeah.
Despite everything, there was a line I couldn't cross.
'This isn't your real family……' No matter what I did, I couldn't get those words out of my head.
I knew I should have been ignoring it, but I just couldn't do it.
I don't know if you'd call it a childhood experience, but it had already become like a curse to me.
Somehow, no matter where I was, I felt like a stranger to my family."
Senpai is silent.
Avoiding my gaze, she huddles her shoulders apologetically.

「んー、基本的に俺はのんびりしてるよ。
できるだけ今を楽しむっていうのを座右の銘にしたからさ。
やっぱり人間、終わっちまった事より先のことを楽しみにしてたほうがハッピーじゃない？」
　まあ、そりゃあ有彦からの受け売りなわけなんだけど。
「先のことを楽しみに、ですか。
いいですね、そういうのって」
　先輩はとても優しい笑顔をしてお茶をすすった。
　こっちも先輩に倣って湯呑みを口にあてる。
　ずず、と渋くてほのかに甘いお茶が喉に流れ落ちていった。
lines.label: s34
lines.maoEnglish:
“Mm, I am easygoing most of the time. I made ‘enjoy the present whenever possible’ my motto. Isn’t it better to look forward to what comes next than to dwell on what’s already over?”
Admittedly, I had stolen that philosophy wholesale from Arihiko.
“Looking forward to what comes next… That sounds lovely.”
Ciel smiled very gently and sipped her tea.
I followed her example and raised my cup.
The tea slid down my throat, bitter with a faint sweetness.

「これからはここから屋敷に帰る道が通学路になるワケか……」

Beyond the front gate, I reached the intersection leading into the residential district.
One road led downtown; the other toward the neighborhood where the estate stood――――
“Oh, it’s Tohno.”
I had run straight into Yumizuka.
“Oh—hello, Yumizuka.”
Maybe because Ciel had teased me about her, I suddenly felt self-conscious.
Yumizuka stared at me in astonishment.

「えーっと、弓塚さん？
　俺の顔に何かついてる？」
「だって、どうして遠野くんがここにいるのかなって。
遠野くんの家、反対方向だよ？」
「あ……まあ、昨日まではそうだったけど、今日からは別だよ。
これからはあっちの住宅地の奥にある、坂の上の家に住む事になったから」
「あ、朝に言ってたのはその事だったんだ」
　ぽん、と手を叩いて納得する弓塚。
　……まあ、お世辞抜きにして、そういう仕草は愛らしいと思う。
lines.label: s35
lines.maoEnglish:
“Um, Yumizuka? Is there something on my face?”
“I was wondering why you were here. Your house is in the opposite direction, isn’t it?”
“Ah—it was until yesterday. Starting today, I’ll be living over there—in the house on the hill beyond the residential district.”
“Oh, so that’s what you were talking about this morning.”
Understanding dawned, and Yumizuka clapped her hands together.
Flattery aside, little gestures like that really were charming.

lines.label: s35
lines.maoEnglish:
“That’s right. You already know, so there’s no point hiding it from you. As of today, I’m leaving the Arimas, who took me in, and moving back to my birth family’s home.”
“Your family home—you mean the Tohno estate?”
“Yes. I know I hardly look as though I belong there.”
“Of course—you’re really the prince on the hill. It used to be a secret only Inui and I knew, but I suppose everyone will find out soon now.”
With a faint smile, Yumizuka let her gaze drift into the distance.
Beyond the sky.
She seemed to be looking toward the Tohno estate high on a faraway hill.

「でも大丈夫？
　自分のお家だって言っても、もう八年も離れているんでしょう？
　その、恐いなー、とか不安だなー、とか思わない？」
「そうだね、実際不安ではあるよ。
もとから俺はあの屋敷が好きじゃなかったし、今じゃ他人の家みたいに感じるしね。
けど、それでも―――」
　……妹である秋葉を一人残したまま、自分だけのんびりと暮らしていくことなんてできない。
　どんなに不安でも、俺は屋敷に戻らないといけないんだ。
lines.label: s35
lines.maoEnglish:
“But will you be all right? It may be your own home, but you’ve been away for eight years. Aren’t you scared or uneasy?”
“I am uneasy, to tell the truth. I never liked that estate to begin with, and now it feels like someone else’s house. Even so―――”
I couldn’t leave my little sister Akiha there alone while I went on living comfortably elsewhere.
However uneasy I might be, I had to return to the estate.

lines.japanese:
「――わたし、ちゃんと憶えてるよ。
　今にして思えばただ倉庫に閉じ込められただけだったんだけど、あの時は寒くて暗くて、すごく不安だった。

lines.maoEnglish:
“――I remember it perfectly.”
“Looking back, we were only locked in a shed, but at the time it was dark and freezing, and we were terrified.

“I see. That sounds awful.”
I still couldn’t quite imagine it, and my answer came out halfhearted.
Yumizuka paid no attention and continued as though the memory remained brilliantly vivid.

lines.japanese:
「そうしてみんなが震えてる時にね、遠野くんがやってきたの。
いつもの、自然で気負ったところのない口調で“中に誰かいるの？
”って。
見てわからないのかーっ、て主将がカンシャクをおこしたの、覚えてる？」
「ああ、それは覚えてる。
ドガンって扉にバットを投げつけた音だろ。
アレ、びっくりしたよ」
　そうそう、と弓塚は笑った。
lines.label: s35
lines.maoEnglish:
“While we were all shivering, you came along. In your usual calm, unruffled voice, you asked, ‘Is anyone in there?’ as though it were nothing. Remember how our captain lost her temper and shouted that it should have been obvious?”
“That I remember. She hurled a bat at the door with a huge bang. It scared the life out of me.”
Yumizuka laughed and agreed.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"And just when everyone was trembling, you came along and asked, 'Is anyone in there?' in your usual unexcited voice… and then the captain got angry and shouted, 'Can't you tell just by looking!?'… Do you remember?"
"Yeah, I remember.
There was a loud bang when she threw a bat at the door.
I was really surprised."
"That's right!" Yumizuka says, laughing.

「でも、先生方はみんな帰ってるって聞いて、わたしたち本当に絶望したんだから。

『内緒にするなら開けられないこともないよ』って」

lines.label: s35
lines.maoEnglish:
“But when you told us all the teachers had left, we despaired. We couldn’t stand another minute, and suddenly we thought we might be trapped there until morning.
Just when we had abandoned all hope, someone tapped on the door. Then you said you might be able to open it if we promised to keep it secret.”
“Right. Then there was another tremendous bang.
Your captain was furious. She screamed that if it were that easy, we would not have been in that mess.”

“See? So if I ever find myself in trouble again, you’ll save me then too, won’t you?”
Yumizuka asked with a smile.

lines.label: s35
lines.maoEnglish:
Honestly, that put me in a difficult position.
I wasn’t capable of everything Yumizuka imagined.
Even so, with her smiling at me like that, I didn’t want to betray her trust.

「うん。
ありがとう、遠野くん。
随分と遅れちゃったけど、あの時の遠野くんの言葉、嬉しかった」
　言って、弓塚の足がぴたりと止まった。
　つられてこっちの足も止まる。
lines.label: s35
lines.maoEnglish:
“All right. If it’s within my power, I’ll help.”
“Thank you, Tohno. I know it’s terribly late to say it. But what you said that day made me happy.”
With that, Yumizuka stopped dead.
I stopped beside her without thinking.

　それは、どこか思いつめたような声だった。
　夕焼けの赤色のせいか、弓塚はどことなく寂しそうに、見える。
「……なにいってるんだ。
話なんていつでもできるよ」
「だめだよ。
遠野くんには乾くんがいるから。
それに、わたしは遠野くんみたいになれないもの」
　遠慮がちに返答して、弓塚は俺から離れていく。
lines.label: s35
lines.maoEnglish:
“I’ve always wished I could talk with you like this.”
She sounded as though she had been carrying those words for a long time.
Perhaps it was only the red of sunset, but Yumizuka looked somehow lonely.
“What are you talking about? We can talk whenever you want.”
“No, we can’t. You have Inui. Besides, I could never be like you.”
Yumizuka answered hesitantly and drew away from me.

lines.japanese:
いつもとは違う帰り道を歩く。
　見知らぬ道を通り抜けて、段々と遠野の屋敷へ近付いていく。
　まわりの風景は、知らない風景ではなかった。
　少なくとも自分は八年前───九歳まで遠野の屋敷で暮らしていたから、屋敷へ帰る道は初めてというわけでもないのだ。
　……少しだけ気持ちは複雑だ。
　この帰り道は懐かしくて、新鮮でもある。
　さっきまで遠野の家に戻るのは気が進まなかったっていうのに、今はそれほどイヤでもなくなっている。
lines.label: s36
lines.maoEnglish:
I followed a different road home than usual.
Unknown streets carried me steadily closer to the Tohno estate.
Yet the scenery around them was not entirely unfamiliar.
I had lived at the estate until I was nine───eight years ago, so this was not truly my first journey home.
My feelings were complicated.
The road seemed nostalgic and new at once.
Only a little while ago, I had dreaded returning to the Tohno home, but now the prospect no longer seemed so unpleasant.

　俺を嫌っていた父親───遠野家の当主である遠野槙久は、先日他界したという。

The house where Shiki Tohno had lived until the age of nine.
An absurdly out-of-place mansion built in the Western style stood there, and I had been told my younger sister Akiha still lived there.
My father, who had hated me───Makihisa Tohno, the head of the Tohno family—was said to have died only recently.

遠野家の跡取りになる、という事はがんじがらめの教育を受けるという事だ。
　それがイヤで自由に暮らしていて、父親から何度小言を言われたかわからない。
　そんな折、俺は事故に巻き込まれて病弱な体になってしまい、父親はこれ幸いにと俺を切り捨てた。
　父親曰く『たとえ長男であろうと、いつ死ぬかわからない者を後継者にはできん』とかなんとか。
　あいにく父親の予想を裏切って回復してしまったけれど、その頃には遠野家の跡取りは妹の秋葉に決められていた。
lines.label: s36
lines.maoEnglish:
Becoming the Tohno heir meant submitting to an education that bound you hand and foot.
I hated that and lived as freely as I could, earning more lectures from my father than I could count.
Then I was caught in the accident and left sickly, and my father seized the opportunity to cast me aside. His explanation was something like, “Eldest son or not, I cannot make an heir of someone who might die at any moment.”
Unfortunately for him, I recovered, but by then my sister Akiha had been chosen to inherit the Tohno family.

lines.mirrorMoon:
To become the Tohno heir means being bound by a strict upbringing.
I have lost count of the number of times my father scolded me over my dislike of not being able to live freely.
That was when I got involved in that accident, and my body became weakened… My father saw it as a good opportunity to get rid of me.
His reasoning was something along the lines of "someone who could die any moment can't become the heir, even if he is the eldest son".
Sadly for my father, I betrayed his expectations by making a recovery, but my sister Akiha was already deemed to be the heir to the Tohno household.

It had been eight years, so my memory was vague, but there had been other children around my age at the estate.

名前までは思い出せないけど、たしか双子の女の子だった。
　身寄りがなくて、使用人として働くことを前提に引き取った、と親父は話していた。
「……おかしいな。
子供のころは三人でよく遊んだのに、名前が思い出せないなんて」
　目を閉じて思い返す。
lines.label: s39
lines.maoEnglish:
I couldn’t remember their names, but I thought they were twin girls.
Father had said they had no family and had been taken in on the understanding that they would work as servants.
“How strange. We played together constantly, yet I can’t remember their names.”
I closed my eyes and searched my memory.

I close my eyes and cast my mind back.

たしかに思い出せる。
　いつも明るくて、見ているだけでこっちまで元気になってくるような女の子だった。
　屈託のない性格で、屋敷のみんなから可愛がられていた女の子。
　歳が近いっていう事もあって、俺とこの子はすごく気が合って、毎日のように庭を走りまわっていた。
『志貴ちゃん、いっしょにあそぼ』
　なんて言って、部屋に閉じこもっていた自分を外に連れ出してくれたのを、覚えている。
lines.label: s39
lines.maoEnglish:
Yes, I could remember one of them clearly.
She was always cheerful; simply looking at her filled me with energy.
Everyone at the estate adored her for her bright, untroubled nature.
We were close in age and got along wonderfully, racing through the gardens together almost every day.
‘Shiki, come play with me’
she would say, drawing me outside whenever I shut myself in my room.

lines.mirrorMoon:
I should be able to remember.
She was a girl who was always cheerful… so cheerful that you would become cheerful just by looking at her.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: Shiki says that this much he can indeed remember before giving a vivid portrait of the cheerful twin. 'Should be able to' instead suggests that the memory is presently inaccessible, weakening the deliberate contrast between what he remembers clearly and the names and identities he cannot recover.

Perhaps she had actually been older than the rest of us.
She would gather us together and make sure Akiha joined in, but once we began playing, she stepped back a little and watched over us.
Even the stern steward responsible for Akiha’s education once relented and said, ‘As long as ――― is with you, I suppose it is all right,’ before allowing Akiha outside.

　少女は、決して屋敷から外に出ようとはしなかった。
　ただ冷たい目をして、ずっと俺たちのことを眺めているだけ。
lines.label: s39
lines.maoEnglish:
She was the cheerful girl’s twin, yet she always watched us without expression.
She never once tried to leave the mansion.
She merely stood there, gazing down at us with cold eyes.

　そんな事を思いだしつつ、鞄から白いリボンを取り出す。
　古びた白いリボン。
　最後に、彼女たちから渡されたもの。
lines.label: s39
lines.maoEnglish:
“I wonder if those girls are still at the estate…”
As the memories returned, I took a white ribbon from my bag.
An old white ribbon.
Something the girls had given me at the very end.

　……貸してあげるから、返してね。
　たしかそんなふうな事を言って、女の子は走り去っていった。

　あとは誰の見送りもなく、有間のおばさんに手を引かれて、あのだだっ広い屋敷の正門をくぐり抜けた。
　それが八年前、遠野の屋敷を後にする時の最後の記憶。
lines.label: s39
lines.maoEnglish:
A servant found me soon afterward and took me to the entrance hall, with no one else there to see me off.
My aunt from the Arima family took me by the hand, and together we passed through the gates of that immense estate.
That was my final memory of leaving the Tohno estate eight years ago.

　あまつさえ、どっちの子がリボンを渡してくれたのかさえ定かじゃない。
lines.label: s39
lines.maoEnglish:
“Whew.”
I sighed and returned the ribbon to my bag.
“But that was eight years ago.”
I didn’t know whether the girl was still at the estate or even remember her name.
Worse, I was no longer certain which of the twins had given me the ribbon.

　けど、覚えているかぎりは守りたい。
　こうして屋敷に戻ることを承諾したのは秋葉が一人きりで屋敷にいるからだ。
　八年間もアイツを放っておいて、全ての責任をあいつに押しつけて勝手気侭に暮らしていた自分に負い目があるから屋敷に戻る。
　……そのついでというワケじゃないけど。
　まだ屋敷にあの子が残っているのなら、八年前の約束をキチンとはたしてあげたかった。
lines.label: s39
lines.maoEnglish:
“It wasn’t an important promise, so I suppose it hardly matters.”
Still, as long as I remembered it, I wanted to keep it.
I had agreed to return because Akiha was alone at the estate.
I had abandoned her for eight years, leaving every responsibility on her shoulders while I lived however I pleased; the guilt of that was what called me back to the estate.
Returning the ribbon was not exactly an afterthought.
If that girl was still at the estate, I wanted to keep the promise I had made eight years ago.

有間の家に預けられた当初、秋葉は何度か訪ねにきてくれたらしい。
　あいにくとこっちは病院通いの毎日で会う事もできず、秋葉が全寮制のお嬢様学校に進学してからはまったく連絡をとっていなかった。
　自分は秋葉とは違い、本家から外れた人間だ。
　だからこうして自由気ままな生活を送れている。
　高校もあくまで平均的な進学校で、ここ八年ばかり妹との接点は皆無といってよかった。

lines.maoEnglish:

Unfortunately, I spent nearly every day at the hospital and never managed to see her; after she entered an exclusive girls’ boarding school, we lost contact altogether.
Unlike Akiha, I had been cast out of the main Tohno family.
That was why I could live as I pleased. I attended an ordinary college-preparatory high school, and for the past eight years, my sister and I had shared virtually nothing.

　子供の頃。
　秋葉は大人しくて、いつも何かを我慢しているように怯えていて、トコトコと足音をたてて俺の後についてきた。
　長い黒髪と豪華な洋服のせいか、秋葉は本当にフランス人形のように儚げな少女だったっけ。

lines.maoEnglish:
After Father died, word came that I was to return to the estate.
Frankly, I had no intention of going back to the Tohno family after all this time.
But Akiha was there.
When we were children.
Akiha was quiet and timid, forever as though she were holding something back; she would patter along behind me wherever I went.
Perhaps it was the long black hair and elaborate Western dresses, but she had seemed as fragile as a porcelain doll.

lines.japanese:
外はすでに日が落ちている。
　ぼんやりと電灯の点った長い廊下を、メイド服の女の子が無言で歩いている。
「……なんか、おとぎの国みたいだ」
　思わずそんな感想を洩らす。
「志貴さま、何かおっしゃられましたか？」
　立ち止まって振りかえる翡翠。
lines.label: s40
lines.maoEnglish:
The sun had already set.
A girl in a maid’s uniform walked wordlessly down a long corridor lit by dim electric lamps.
“It’s like something out of a fairy tale.”
The thought escaped my lips.
“Did you say something, Master Shiki?”
Hisui stopped and looked back.

「……俺の部屋って、ここ？」
「はい。
ご不満がおありでしたら違うお部屋をご用意させていただきますが」
「いや、不満なんてあるわけないけど、その――」
　ちょっと、いやかなり立派すぎるかなって。
「志貴さま？」
「―――いいんだ、なんでもない。
喜んでこの部屋を使わせてもらうよ」

“This is my room?”

“No, there’s nothing to dislike; it’s just――”

“Master Shiki?”
“―――Never mind; it’s nothing. I’ll be delighted to use this room.”

「はい。
お部屋は八年前から手を加えていませんので、不具合はないと思います」
「―――？」

「……ねえ。

「そう伺っておりますが、違うのですか？」

lines.maoEnglish:
“Very good. Nothing in the room has been changed in eight years, so I do not expect any inconvenience.”
“―――?”
There was something odd about the way Hisui had put that.
She made it sound as though this had once been my room.
“…Was this my room before I left?”
“That is what I was told, but was it not?”
Hisui tilted her head ever so slightly.
What a relief.
Apparently she did possess some means of expressing emotion.

「……まあ、言われてみればそうかもしれない。
少しは覚えがあるし、きっとそうだったんだろう」
　親近感はまったく湧かないけど、八年間も離れていればそんなものなのかもしれない。
「けど、やっぱり落ち着かないな。
今朝まで六畳半の部屋で暮らしてたからさ、なんだか高級ホテルに泊まりに来たみたいだ」
「お気持ちはわかりますが、どうかお慣れください。
志貴さまは今日から遠野家のご長男なのですから」
lines.label: s40
lines.maoEnglish:
“Now that you mention it, perhaps it was. A few things do seem familiar, so I suppose that must be right.”
The room stirred no affection in me at all, but perhaps eight years away would do that.
“Still, I can’t relax here. Until this morning I lived in a cramped six-and-a-half-mat room; this feels like checking into a luxury hotel.”
“I understand, but please try to become accustomed to it. As of today, Master Shiki is once again the eldest son of the Tohno family.”

「そうだね。
せめて外見ぐらいは笑われないように頑張ってみるよ」
　トン、と机に鞄を置いて背筋を伸ばす。
―――色々と神経がまいりそうだけど、たしかに今日から慣れていくしかないだろう。
lines.label: s40
lines.maoEnglish:
“You’re right. I’ll at least try to look the part well enough not to be laughed at.”
I set my bag on the desk with a thump and straightened my back.
―――This place was going to wear my nerves thin, but from today on, I would simply have to get used to it.

時計は夕方の六時をまわったあたり。
　いつもなら居間にいってテレビでも見てる時間だけど、この屋敷にそんなものがあるかどうか真剣に疑わしい。

Ordinarily I would be in the living room watching television, but I had serious doubts that the estate contained one.

“Wait. Which relatives were ‘staying’ here, and for how long?”
“The family of the eldest son of the Kugamine branch; the Tosaki family’s third daughter and her fiancé; and the Kishima family’s eldest son. They stayed for roughly three years.”
“Three years? Hisui, I think the word for that is freeloading, not staying.”
Hisui did not answer.
No matter what those freeloaders had been like, a servant could hardly speak ill of them.

“The family of the eldest son of the Kugamine branch; the Tosaki family’s third daughter and her fiancé; and the Kishima family’s eldest son. They stayed for roughly three years.”
“Three years? Hisui, I think the word for that is freeloading, not staying.”
Hisui did not answer.
No matter what those freeloaders had been like, a servant could hardly speak ill of them.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Hold on.
Visitors?
Like who?
For how long?"
"Relatives.
The eldest son of Kugamine-sama from a branch of the family, Touzaki-sama's third daughter and her fiance, and Kishima-sama's eldest son came to stay for close to three years."
"…… Three years, huh?
Hisui, that's what you'd call freeloaders, not visitors."
Hisui does not reply.
No matter what kind of people these freeloaders were, it seems that servants can't say anything bad about them.

lines.japanese:
まあ、ともかく逗留していた親戚筋の連中は自分たちの荷物を持ちかえらされたという事らしい。
　となると、あの現代的な文化ってモノを俗物的と毛嫌いしていた父親がテレビなんて観るはずもない。
　父親のもとで八年間も躾けられた秋葉も同じだろう。
lines.label: s40
lines.maoEnglish:
At any rate, Akiha had evidently made the resident relatives take their possessions with them.
Father had despised modern culture as hopelessly vulgar, so he certainly would never have watched television.
After eight years under his discipline, Akiha was probably the same.

lines.mirrorMoon:

Akiha, who had been educated by him for the last eight years, would probably be the same.

lines.japanese:
「───ま、ないからって別に死ぬわけでもないか」
　翡翠は黙っている。
　……使用人の鑑というか、翡翠は聞かれた事以外は何も喋らない。
　当然、こっちとしては気が滅入る。
　なんとかしてこの無表情な顔を笑わせてみたいと思うのだけど、どうも生半可な努力では不可能そうではある。
lines.label: s40
lines.maoEnglish:
“───Well, I’m not going to die without one.”
Hisui remained silent.
The perfect servant, perhaps: she never said anything she had not been asked.
Naturally, that left me feeling rather low.
I wanted to find some way of making that blank face smile, but no ordinary effort was likely to succeed.

「───翡翠？」
　翡翠はうんとも言わない。
　と、突然まっすぐにこちらを見据えてきた。
「姉さんの部屋になら、あると思います」
「は？」
　いやもう、ワケがわからない。
「……えーっと。
あるって、何が」
「ですからテレビです。
以前、姉さんの部屋で見かけた記憶がありますから」
　翡翠はまるで数年前の出来事を思い出すように言った。
lines.label: s40
lines.maoEnglish:
“───Hisui?”
She did not so much as murmur.
Then, without warning, her gaze fixed directly on me.
“I believe there is one in my sister’s room.”
“What?”
Now I was completely lost.
“…There’s what in her room?”
“A television. I remember seeing one there before.”
Hisui spoke as though she were recalling something from years ago.

「ちょっと待って。
姉さんって、もしかして琥珀さんのこと？」
「はい。
現在、このお屋敷で働かせていただいている者はわたしと姉さんの二人きりです」

lines.maoEnglish:
“Wait. By your sister, do you mean Kohaku?”
“Yes. My sister and I are currently the only two servants employed at this estate.”
Now that she mentioned it, they did look alike. Kohaku’s perpetual smile and Hisui’s blank face had kept me from thinking of them as sisters.
“I see. Kohaku certainly seems like the sort to watch variety shows.”
Even so, barging into Kohaku’s room and asking to watch her television felt rather presumptuous.

I would simply become the diligent student worthy of the Tohno family.

lines.japanese:
「――――――――でかい」
　正門について、ついそんな言葉が口に出た。
　一般家庭に慣れしたんだ自分にとって、遠野の屋敷は大きく現実からかけ離れてしまっている。
「………早まったかな、俺」
　……いや、今さら後悔しても始まらない。
　門は開いている。
　力任せに押しあけて、屋敷の玄関へと向かっていった。
lines.label: s41
lines.maoEnglish:
“――――――――It’s enormous.”
The words escaped me when I reached the main gate.
After growing accustomed to an ordinary household, the Tohno estate seemed impossibly vast, almost divorced from reality.
“Maybe coming back was a mistake.”
No—regret would accomplish nothing now.
The gate stood unlocked.
I heaved it open and headed for the estate’s front entrance.

The gates aren't locked.
I push them open, and head towards the mansion doors.

lines.japanese:
屋敷の玄関は重苦しくそびえ、訪れる者を威圧している。
　両開きの扉の横には、不釣り合いな呼び鈴があった。
「…………よし」
　緊張を振り払って呼び鈴を押す。
　ぴんぽーん、なんていう親しみのある音はしない。
　重苦しい静寂が続くこと数秒。
　扉の奥でぱたぱた、という慌ただしい人の気配がした。
lines.label: s41
lines.maoEnglish:
The estate’s front entrance loomed above me, ponderous and forbidding.
Beside the massive double doors was a doorbell that looked almost comically out of place.
“All right.”
Shaking off my nerves, I pressed it.
No friendly little chime answered me.
Several seconds passed in oppressive silence.
Then came the hurried patter of someone beyond the doors.

lines.mirrorMoon:

There isn't any affectionate "ding-dong" chime from the doorbell.
The oppressive silence continues for a few seconds.
Then, the sound of pattering footsteps behind the door indicates someone's presence.

Beyond it were a familiar entrance hall and a girl in an old-fashioned house apron.

lines.japanese:
「よかった。
あんまりに遅いから迷っているのかなって心配しちゃってたんですよ。
日が落ちてもいらっしゃらなかったらお迎えに行こうかなって思ってたんですから」
　割烹着なんていうアナクロなものを着込んだ少女はにこにこと笑っている。
「あ、いや───それは、その」
　こちらはというと、少女のあまりに時代錯誤なカッコウに面食らってしまって、まともな言葉が口にできない。
lines.label: s41
lines.maoEnglish:
“Thank goodness. You were so late, I was afraid you’d lost your way. If you hadn’t arrived by sundown, I was going to come and find you.”
The girl, dressed in an old-fashioned, long-sleeved house apron, beamed at me.
“Ah───no, I mean…”
Her hopelessly anachronistic outfit had caught me so far off guard that I could not form a coherent sentence.

lines.maoEnglish:
Perhaps puzzled by my stammering, she tipped her head slightly.
“You’re Master Shiki, aren’t you?”
“Uh—yes. You can leave off the ‘Master,’ though.”
“I knew it! Oh, please don’t frighten me like that. I thought I’d gotten it wrong again.”
She laughed with easy, unaffected warmth.
I had no proof, but she fit the picture in my memory perfectly.

Akiha gave me another icy look.
Without saying a word, she seemed to hurl eight years of resentment at me for leaving her here alone.

“You don’t want to keep running into relatives in the halls, do you? I dismissed most of the servants as well, but I kept those assigned to us, so there is no problem.”

lines.label: s41
lines.maoEnglish:
“I see. You and I hardly ever spoke. Sorry—I got carried away on my own.”
“Master Shiki has nothing to apologize for. I am the one who behaved discourteously toward Master Shiki, even if I was only a child.”
Hisui bowed deeply.
“――――――”
This was painfully awkward.
I knew she meant no harm, but I had no idea how to respond when a girl about my age spoke to me that way.
“Is there anything else you require, Master Shiki?”
“Ah—no, nothing.”
“Then I will return for you in one hour; until then, please make yourself comfortable.”
Hisui said it all without expression.

lines.japanese:
翡翠はめずらしく困ったような顔をして、視線を宙に泳がした。
「……居間にはありません。
ご逗留の方々はご使用になってらっしゃいましたが、出立される時に荷物はすべてお持ち帰りいただきましたので残ってはいないと思います」
「ちょっと待った。
逗留って、誰がどのくらいしてたのさ」

「分家筋である久我峰さまのご長男のご家族、刀崎さまのご三女とその婚約者、軋間さまのご長男がご逗留なさっていました。
期間は三年ほどです」
「……三年、か。
翡翠、そういうのって逗留っていうんじゃなくて居候って言うんじゃない？」
　翡翠は答えない。
　居候していた連中がどんな人間であろうと、使用人である以上失礼な事は言えないみたいだ。

まあ、ともかく逗留していた親戚筋の連中は自分たちの荷物を持ちかえらされたという事らしい。
　となると、あの現代的な文化ってモノを俗物的と毛嫌いしていた父親がテレビなんて観るはずもない。
　父親のもとで八年間も躾けられた秋葉も同じだろう。
lines.label: s41
lines.maoEnglish:
For once, Hisui looked uncertain as her gaze drifted into the air.
“There is none in the sitting room. Some of the relatives staying here had televisions, but they took all their belongings when they departed, so I do not believe any remain.”
“Wait. Which relatives were ‘staying’ here, and for how long?”
“The family of the eldest son of the Kugamine branch; the Tosaki family’s third daughter and her fiancé; and the Kishima family’s eldest son. They stayed for roughly three years.”
“Three years? Hisui, I think the word for that is freeloading, not staying.”
Hisui did not answer.
No matter what those freeloaders had been like, a servant could hardly speak ill of them.
At any rate, Akiha had evidently made the resident relatives take their possessions with them.
Father had despised modern culture as hopelessly vulgar, so he certainly would never have watched television.
After eight years under his discipline, Akiha was probably the same.

But I’m fine now. I still get light-headed sometimes—about once a month—but I’m not so frail that you need to worry about me.”

Akiha nodded gravely.

“――――――”
…Of course—Akiha knew neither that I had begun wearing glasses nor why.
But there was no way I could explain that I saw ‘lines’ along which things broke, or that the glasses kept me from seeing them.

“Really? You seemed remarkably calm for someone so surprised.”
“――Naturally. I could hardly disgrace myself when meeting you again after eight years.”
Akiha huffed and knitted her brows in displeasure.

Akiha and Kohaku seemed to be heading for the baths, so perhaps I should return to my room.

こっちの記憶の中じゃ秋葉は大人しくて、いつも不安げな瞳で俺のあとをついてくる一歳年下の妹だった。
　子供の頃の秋葉は無口で、自分のやりたい事も口にだせないほど弱気で、いつも父親である遠野槙久に叱られないかっておどおどしていた線の細い女の子だったのに。
「───そうだよな。
八年も経てば人間だってガラリと変わる」

lines.label: s43
lines.maoEnglish:
In my memories, Akiha was my quiet little sister, one year younger, always trailing behind me with anxious eyes.
As a child she had been frail and timid, too shy even to say what she wanted, forever frightened that her father, Makihisa Tohno, might scold her.
“───Of course. Eight years is enough to change anyone completely.”
Just as those eight years had made me into Shiki Tohno,
they must have made Akiha into Akiha Tohno as well.

She's not some upper-class lady or anything, so why should she have to do something as bothersome as---
"…… Oh wait, she is an upper-class lady."
Yes.
Come to think of it, my sister, Tohno Akiha, is a natural born upper-class lady.

lines.japanese:
こっちの記憶の中じゃ秋葉は大人しくて、いつも不安げな瞳で俺のあとをついてくる一歳年下の妹だった。
　子供の頃の秋葉は無口で、自分のやりたい事も口にだせないほど弱気で、いつも父親である遠野槙久に叱られないかっておどおどしていた線の細い女の子だったのに。
「───そうだよな。
八年も経てば人間だってガラリと変わる」
　自分が八年間で今の遠野志貴になったように、
　秋葉もこの八年間で今の遠野秋葉になったんだろう。
lines.label: s44
lines.maoEnglish:
In my memories, Akiha was my quiet little sister, one year younger, always trailing behind me with anxious eyes.
As a child she had been frail and timid, too shy even to say what she wanted, forever frightened that her father, Makihisa Tohno, might scold her.
“───Of course. Eight years is enough to change anyone completely.”
Just as those eight years had made me into Shiki Tohno,
they must have made Akiha into Akiha Tohno as well.

　知らず、そんな謝罪の言葉を呟いた。
lines.label: s44
lines.maoEnglish:
―――Eight years is a long time.
Half my life so far.
I had been absent from this house during the years that mattered most—the years when a child struggled to become an adult.
“I’m sorry, Akiha.”
If only I could have been there beside her through those eight years.
The thought brought the apology unbidden to my lips.

　コンコン、と扉をノックする。

　待つ事三分弱。
　扉が開いて琥珀さんが顔を出してきた。

I knocked twice.
“Kohaku, are you in there?”
“Coming—just a minute!”
Her cheerful voice floated through the door.
I waited just under three minutes.
The door opened and Kohaku poked her head out.

“Um, well―――I thought perhaps I could watch television with you.”
“Huh?”
Kohaku stared at me, blinking in astonishment.

Just look at Kohaku: she was still staring, appalled by my behavior—or perhaps not.

Kohaku beamed at me.

lines.maoEnglish:
“You came for television, didn’t you? What does Master Shiki usually watch at this hour?”
“Nothing in particular; mostly the news, I suppose. I’m a sucker for whatever is current, especially fashionable nonsense.”
“Really? Master Shiki seems so composed that I imagined you spent your evenings reading.”
“Ahaha, I’m not nearly that refined, and I don’t think I’m particularly composed either. Maybe the glasses just give people that impression.”

“A meticulous random attacker. Isn’t that a contradiction? These attacks are supposed to be crimes of impulse.”

“I’ll be perfectly safe. The attacker only appears after midnight. If I stay indoors at night, I’ll never encounter the attacker.”
Kohaku’s reasoning was beautifully simple.
The murders felt too immediate for such detachment, but perhaps that was what every tragedy on the news became to people watching from home.

こっちの記憶の中じゃ秋葉は大人しくて、いつも不安げな瞳で俺のあとをついてくる一歳年下の妹だった。
　子供の頃の秋葉は無口で、自分のやりたい事も口にだせないほど弱気で、いつも父親である遠野槙久に叱られないかっておどおどしていた線の細い女の子だったのに。
「───そうだよな。
八年も経てば人間だってガラリと変わる」
　自分が八年間で今の遠野志貴になったように、
　秋葉もこの八年間で今の遠野秋葉になったんだろう。
lines.label: s45
lines.maoEnglish:
In my memories, Akiha was my quiet little sister, one year younger, always trailing behind me with anxious eyes.
As a child she had been frail and timid, too shy even to say what she wanted, forever frightened that her father, Makihisa Tohno, might scold her.
“───Of course. Eight years is enough to change anyone completely.”
Just as those eight years had made me into Shiki Tohno,
they must have made Akiha into Akiha Tohno as well.

With my own family for the first time in eight years.
Yet I felt as though I were in a stranger’s house.
“Haaah… what’s going to happen to me now?”
With no one there to hear me complain, I drifted into sleep.

　遠吠えは夜に響く。
　音は、間違いなく屋敷の右手側のほうから聞こえてくる。
lines.label: s47a
lines.maoEnglish:

There could be no mistake: it was coming from the right side of the estate.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirror_moon:

　屋敷の周り、高い壁が延々と続く夜道。
　喉をならしながら、犬たちが集まっている場所へ歩いていった。
lines.label: s47a
lines.maoEnglish:
“……”
For some reason my throat had gone dry.
Outside the estate, the high wall stretched endlessly along the night road.
Swallowing against the dryness, I followed it toward the place where the dogs had gathered.

「……あれ？」
　オーーーーーーーーーン。
　鳴き声は依然としてやまない。
　なのに、そこに犬の姿なんてなかった。
　あるのは―――人影だけだ。
　ぽつん、と闇をきりとったような街灯の明かりの下、黒いコートの男が立っている。
　遠吠えは、男の側から聞こえている。
―――――だが、犬の姿などどこにもない。
lines.label: s47a

“Huh…?”
Awooooooooooo.
The howling had not stopped.
Yet there was not a dog in sight.
There was only―――a human figure.
A man in a black coat stood alone beneath a streetlamp, its island of light cut from the darkness.
The howling came from beside the man.
―――――Yet there was no dog anywhere.

―――And then.
The crow abruptly vanishes.

lines.label: s47a

“Why am I shaking…?”
My fingers were trembling.
My whole body shuddered in tiny spasms, and an unnatural cold ran down my back.
If I had to compare it to something—yes.
It felt as though someone had torn out my spinal cord and driven a pillar of ice into its place.

Getting out of bed, I slip out of the room quietly.
lines.mirror_moon:
"------?"
I hear it again.
…… Inside the mansion… from the lobby?
"-----Could it be a burglar?"
It's not impossible.
The mansion's contents are outrageously valuable.
On top of that, with no one here now except Kohaku-san, Hisui, Akiha and myself, it's very insecure.
"……"
Getting out of bed, I slip out of the room quietly.

lines.japanese:
……もし泥棒だったら秋葉たちが危ないし、こればっかりは見過ごしておけない。
　二階からロビーの様子を眺めるだけなら、こっちにも危険はないと思う。
lines.label: s48
lines.maoEnglish:
If it was a burglar, Akiha and the others might be in danger, and I could not ignore that.
Watching the foyer from the second floor should not put me at any risk.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
If it's a burglar, Akiha and everyone will be in danger, so I can't let this one go.
I'll just look down from the second floor into the lobby; that should be safe enough.
lines.mirror_moon:

I'll just look down from the second floor into the lobby; that should be safe enough.

lines.japanese:
……ロビーには異状はない。
「……………！」
　いや、誰かいる。
　玄関から入ってきて、ふらふらとおぼつかない足取りでロビーを横切っていく姿は―――
「あき……は？」
　秋葉は二階の自分の部屋にではなく、一階の西館へ歩いていく。
　その先にあるものは琥珀さんの部屋と、親父の部屋ぐらいのものだ。
lines.label: s48
lines.maoEnglish:
Nothing seemed amiss in the foyer.
“……!”
No—someone was there.
A figure had entered through the front door and was staggering unsteadily across the foyer—
“Aki—ha?”
Instead of going upstairs to her room, Akiha headed into the west wing on the ground floor.
The only rooms that way were Kohaku’s and Father’s.

lines.japanese:
「……なにしてたんだ、アイツ。
こんな夜更けに……」
　呟いてみても答えはない。
　しばらくロビーの様子を眺めてから、大人しく自分の部屋に戻ることにした。
lines.label: s48
lines.maoEnglish:
“……What was she doing out this late?”
The empty foyer offered no answer.
After watching for a while longer, I returned quietly to my room.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:

lines.japanese:
……まあ、何か用事があったのか、それとも琥珀さんに会いにいったのかもしれない。
　こっちもこっそり盗み見ていたという負い目もあるし、あれこれ詮索するのも気が引ける。
「……寝よ寝よ。
明日も学校だ」
　ベッドにもぐりこんで、目を閉じる。
―――眠りに落ちる途中。
　ロビーで見かけた、うつろな瞳をした秋葉の姿が、なにかよくない物のように、何度も何度も思い返されていた。
lines.label: s48
lines.maoEnglish:
Perhaps she had some errand, or had gone to see Kohaku.
I felt guilty enough for spying on her, so prying any further seemed wrong.
“Back to bed. I have school tomorrow.”
I crawled beneath the covers and closed my eyes.
―――As I drifted back to sleep.
The image of Akiha crossing the foyer with vacant eyes returned again and again, like a glimpse of something ill-omened.

lines.mirrorMoon:
…… Well, she probably had something to do, or went to see Kohaku-san.
I feel bad about sneaking around and watching her, and I don't want to just ask her about everything she does.
"…… Sleep, sleep.
There's school tomorrow."
I bury myself in bed and close my eyes.
---As I fall asleep,
my thoughts keep returning over and over to Akiha's hollow-eyed figure in the lobby… and how something seemed wrong.

lines.japanese:
犬の遠吠えはまだ続いている。
　このままじゃはっきりいって眠れない。
　……眠れないけど、まあ、それは常人の神経のレヴェルの話。
「………………眠いので、パス」
　シーツをかぶって、ベッドに横になる。
　犬の遠吠えなんて、道を走る自動車の音だと思えばいい。
lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
The dogs were still howling.
There was no way anyone could sleep through this.
That was true only for someone with normal nerves.
“I’m too sleepy, so I’ll pass.”
I pulled the sheet over my head and lay down.
I could pretend the howling was only traffic passing on the road.

lines.mirrorMoon:

I can just think of the howling as the sound of something mundane, like cars driving by on the street.

lines.japanese:
「………はあ」
　今日はなんだか長い一日だった。
　慣れない屋敷での夕食や秋葉たちとの会話で精神もつかれきってる。
　その前には犬の遠吠えなんて、ただの雑音に他ならない。
　目を閉じてしまえば、あとはゆるやかに眠りの中へと落ちていけた。
lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
“Haa…”
It had been an awfully long day.
Dinner in the unfamiliar estate and all those conversations with Akiha and the others had exhausted me.
After all that, the dogs were nothing but background noise.
Once I closed my eyes, I slipped gently into sleep.

I close my eyes and gently fall asleep.

lines.japanese:
――――懐かしい、夢を見た。
　八年前の夏の終わり。
　大きなケガをして、誰も来ない病院にうつされて、先生に出会ったあと。
　屋敷に帰ってきた自分は、そこで、知らない家に預けられるという事を、父親の口から聞いた。
　ことは、すごくあっけなかった。
　退院した次の日、自分は有間の家に行くことになったから。
lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
――――I dreamed an old, familiar dream.
It was the end of summer, eight years ago.
After my terrible injury, after they transferred me to a hospital where no one came to visit, after I met Teach.
When I returned to the estate, Father told me I was being sent to live with a family I had never met.
It all happened with startling abruptness.
The day after I left the hospital, I was sent to live with the Arimas.

lines.mirrorMoon:

Everything happened so fast.
Right after the day I left the hospital, I ended up going to the Arima household.

lines.japanese:
それは、雲一つない青空だったのを、覚えている。
　秋の始まり。
　自分は手をひかれて遠野の屋敷を後にした。
　けど、そのほんの少し前。
　あの子が、大人たちの目を盗んで会いに来てくれた。
lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
I remember the sky was blue and utterly cloudless.
Autumn was just beginning.
Someone took my hand and led me away from the Tohno estate.
But shortly before I left.
That girl slipped past the adults and came to see me.

lines.mirrorMoon:

The start of autumn.
I was led away from the Tohno mansion.
But a little before that…
That girl had come to see me, sneaking past the eyes of the adults.

lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
She had asked me to come to the tree in the back garden when it was time to leave,
so I slipped away from Father and went there.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"When you are about to leave, please come to the tree in the rear courtyard."
After being told that, I snuck out from under my old man's eye and out to the rear courtyard.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
青い空。
　どこまでも落ちていけそうな青い空の下、彼女は一人で待っていた。
　自分が知るかぎり、あの子が屋敷から外に出たのは、これが初めてだった気がする。
lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
The blue sky.
Beneath a blue sky that seemed deep enough to fall into forever, she waited alone.
As far as I knew, it was the first time she had ever ventured outside the mansion.

As far as I knew, this was the first time she had left the mansion to come outside.

『これ、持っていって』
　言って、少女は自分の髪を留めていたリボンをほどいて手渡してくれた。
　餞別だったのだろうけど、なにぶん子供だった自分は、嬉しいともかんじない。
　……だって、リボンをもらって喜ぶ九歳の男の子はいないと思う。
lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
She told me to take it;
the girl untied the ribbon from her hair and placed it in my hand.
It must have been a parting gift, but I was only a child and felt no particular joy in it.
After all, I doubt any nine-year-old boy would be delighted to receive a ribbon.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Take this."
Saying that, she undid the ribbon that bound her hair and handed it to me.
I guess it was her farewell gift to me, but as a child, I didn't even feel happy about it.
…… After all, what kind of a nine year old boy would feel happy about receiving a ribbon?

『そのリボンお気に入りなの。
だから、あとでちゃんと返してね』
　けど、その言葉で、救われた。
　返してね、と少女はいった。
　帰ってきてね、と自分には聞こえた。
――――それだけで、よかった。
　誰一人として見送りさえしてくれなかった最後の日。
　今まで一度も話したことがなくっても、彼女がそう言ってくれたのが、嬉しかった。
lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
“That ribbon is my favorite, so make sure you return it to me later.”
Those words saved me.
Return it to me, the girl said.
Return to me, I heard.
――――That alone was enough.
It was the last day, and not one person came to see me off.
I was glad she had said it—even though we had never spoken before.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"That ribbon is my favorite, so give it back to me later, okay?"
But those were the words that saved me.
"Give it back," she said.
"Come back," is what I heard from those words.
---Just that was good enough for me.
That last day, with no one to even see me off.
For her, who I had never even spoken to, to say that to me… it made me happy.

―――けど、きっと返すよ、とは言えなかった。
　こんな時にかぎって利口な自分は、もうこの屋敷に帰ってこれることはないって理解してしまっていたんだろう。
　……交わした言葉は、ただそれだけ。
　少女の氷のような目は、けど、どこか哀しかった。
　時間だから、と玄関へと歩いていく。
　少女は、やっぱり人形みたいに立ち尽くして、去り行く自分の姿を見つめていた。
lines.label: s49
lines.maoEnglish:
―――But I could not tell her, “I’ll be sure to return it.”
Of course, at a time like that, I had to be clever enough to understand that I would never be allowed to return to this house.
That was all we said.
The girl’s eyes were cold as ice, yet there was something sad in them.
When the time came, I walked back toward the entrance.
She remained where she was, standing like a doll and watching me go.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:

As clever as I was at the time, I realized I would never be able to return to this mansion ever again.
…… Those were the only words we exchanged.
Something about her icy eyes was very sorrowful.
It was time, so I began walking towards the doorway.
The girl just stood there like a doll, watching me leave.

lines.japanese:
あおいそら。

lines.mirrorMoon:

lines.japanese:
やる事もないし、早々に学校を後にする。
　……考えてみれば、こうやって正門から下校するのなんて入学式以来だ。
「これからはここから屋敷に帰る道が通学路になるワケか……」
lines.label: s502
lines.maoEnglish:
With nothing else to do, I left school without lingering.
Come to think of it, I hadn’t gone home through the front gate since the entrance ceremony.
“So this is going to be my route back to the estate from now on…”

…… Come to think of it, I hadn't left the school by the main entrance since the entrance ceremony.
"I guess this'll be the way to and from school from now on since I live in the mansion…"

正門から出て住宅地に通じる交差点に出る。
　ここから街に出るか、屋敷のある住宅地に出るかに別れるのだが――――
「あれ、遠野くんだ」
　ばったり、弓塚に出会ってしまった。
「あれ、弓塚さんだ」
　弓塚が目を白黒させて俺を見ているように、こっちも目を点にしてみたりする。
lines.label: s502
lines.maoEnglish:
Beyond the front gate, I reached the intersection leading into the residential district.
One road led downtown; the other toward the neighborhood where the estate stood――――
“Oh, it’s Tohno.”
I had run straight into Yumizuka.
“Oh, it’s Yumizuka.”
She stared at me wide-eyed, and I stared back in equal surprise.

“Oh, it’s Yumizuka.”

"Hey, it's Yumizuka-san."
Yumizuka-san looked at me, bewildered.

lines.maoEnglish:

“Yes. I know I hardly look as though I belong there.”

Beyond the sky.
She seemed to be looking toward the Tohno estate high on a faraway hill.

Her voice had become remarkably buoyant as she hurried to my side.

lines.japanese:
あれは新年になったばかりの、冬の寒い日だった。
　三が日があけて、有間の家に居づらくなった俺は自分から補習を受けたり、学校に残れるような手伝いを申し出ていた。
　けど、それも夕方の五時頃までだ。
　あたりも暗くなってしまい、学校にいた教師たちも帰るという事で俺は教室から追い出された。
lines.label: s502
lines.maoEnglish:
It was a bitterly cold day just after the New Year.
Once the first three days of the holiday were over, I had grown uncomfortable at the Arimas’ and volunteered for extra lessons and odd jobs that would keep me at school.
But even that only lasted until around five.
Darkness had fallen, and the remaining teachers were leaving, so they chased me out of the classroom.

―――中に誰かいるの？
　そう問いかけてみたら、倉庫の中から数人の女生徒の声が返ってきた。

　どうやっても扉は開かないらしく、できれば先生を呼んで助けてほしい、という。

Nothing they tried would budge the door, so they begged me to find a teacher and get them out.

“――I remember it perfectly.”
“Looking back, we were only locked in a shed, but at the time it was dark and freezing, and we were terrified.

“I see. That sounds awful.”
I still couldn’t quite imagine it, and my answer came out halfhearted.
Yumizuka paid no attention and continued as though the memory remained brilliantly vivid.

lines.japanese:
「そうしてみんなが震えてる時にね、遠野くんがやってきたの。
いつもの、自然で気負ったところのない口調で“中に誰かいるの？
”って。
見てわからないのかーっ、て主将がカンシャクをおこしたの、覚えてる？」
「ああ、それは覚えてる。
ドガンって扉にバットを投げつけた音だろ。
アレ、びっくりしたよ」
　そうそう、と弓塚は笑った。
lines.label: s502
lines.maoEnglish:
“While we were all shivering, you came along. In your usual calm, unruffled voice, you asked, ‘Is anyone in there?’ as though it were nothing. Remember how our captain lost her temper and shouted that it should have been obvious?”
“That I remember. She hurled a bat at the door with a huge bang. It scared the life out of me.”
Yumizuka laughed and agreed.

There was a loud bang when she threw a bat at the door.
I was really surprised."
"That's right!" Yumizuka says, laughing.

"I've become curious about you, Tohno-kun.

lines.label: s89
lines.maoEnglish:
In the end, she delighted in everything I told her.
To my surprise, stories from middle school excited her most; apparently she hadn’t gone on the school trip.
I still remembered how her eyes shone as she said, “It sounds wonderful, everyone traveling together.”
Still, talking by myself for an hour was exhausting.
With her permission, I finally set out for home.

lines.mirrorMoon:
In the end, Senpai was happy to listen no matter what I talked to her about.
It was surprising to see her get so worked up when we were talking about middle school.
Apparently, Senpai had never been on a school trip.
"That sounds nice, everyone going on a trip together," she said, her eyes twinkling.
It was quite an impressive sight.
At any rate, I held a one-sided conversation for an hour, but it made me rather tired.
With Senpai's permission, I decide to head home.
